events.title: Matt Berkeley & The Electronic Folk
events.address: 1337 Grant Ave, San Francisco, CA, 94133, United States
events.description:
A wide-ranging night of musical and comic performances led by Matt Berkeley at Tupelo.
Matt Berkeley & The Electrictronic Folk is a San Francisco Bay Area-based group known for playing a mix of dubfunk Soul music. The band features Matt Berkeley on keyboards and vocals, along with a rotating lineup that includes musicians like Dylan Greengard on guitar and Nate Pedley on bass.

events.title: Manny’s: Conjuring Wonder - Magic Up-Close & Personal
events.address: 3092 16th St, San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
Join us for an intimate experience of incredible close-up magic and mind reading with Magician Dennis Kyriakos.
Mystery and Wonder await!
Tripadvisor’s #1 Show in Berkeley comes to San Francisco! Objects vanish and reappear before your eyes. Uncanny coincidences unfold. Secret thoughts are revealed. You’ll be left charmed, bewildered, and amazed.
Doors 7:15 pm
Show 7:30 – 8:30pm
Conjuring Wonder
Magician Dennis Kyriakos has entertained discerning audiences for the past 30 years with amazing, engaging, high-caliber entertainment at corporate functions and high-end private events from New York City to San Francisco, Las Vegas to Palm Springs, and even Shanghai.

events.title: Love Isn't Blind | Live Comedy/Dating Show | SF
events.description: Category: Community Events / VolunteerismContact Name: Allison GoldbergContact Phone: +1 (646) 457-7443Contact Email: allison@allisongoldberg.comCost: From $23.73Link: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/love-isnt-blind-live-comedydating-show-sf-tickets-2001667208504F*** the apps.Doors at 5:30, show at 7 pm.Four men. One bachelorette. The twist? The men can't speak. Instead, host Allison Goldberg calls their moms and searches their phones.Love Isn't Blind is an elimination-style, live comedy/dating game show - and it's coming to The Foundry in San Francisco on Saturday, October 17.Who it's for:Singles who would rather have their fingernails pulled out than continue swiping.Anyone who wants an inclusive, positive place to meet new people IRL in today's godforsaken world. (And yes, that includes friendships, too!)Couples who want a date night that isn't another dinner, or who love the schadenfreude of watching others date because they're sick f***s. (Or maybe you're a couple who loves love and playing wingperson - there are prizes for that.)We're here for the reality tv lovers, the ones who scream while watching Love Is Blind, the bachelorette parties, the birthdays, the anniversaries, group night out, and so much more.As seen on NBC's California Live, The Tamron Hall Show, in LA Magazine, Time Out, and more. Visit loveisntblind.co!Single? Apply here or grab tix to watch.Taken? Nominate friends or grab tix to watch.Created and hosted by Allison Goldberg.

BATS Improv

Explore the world of improv with Fort Mason Center For Arts & Culture resident organization BATS Improv. Saturday nights and select Sunday nights offer in-person shows at the Bayfront Theatre in Building B.

BATS IMPROV DETAILS

La Vida Loca: An Improvised Telenovela ignites passions on Saturday, September 19 and 26, 2026, 8:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.

Halloween season offers The Improvised Twilight Zone on Saturday, October 3 and 10, 2026. Trick Or Treat: Fun-Size Spooky Scenes rings doorbells on October 17 and 24, 2026. Double Creature: A Horrifying Double Feature stalks the stage on Saturday, October 31, 2026. All shows run 8:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.

Saturdays in November are set for Theatresports, November 7 to 26, 8:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.

The Anniversary Show & Gala Dinner sets up on Friday, November 13, 2026, 6:00 p.m. to 11:00 p.m.

Holiday favorite An Improvised Dickens Musical returns on Saturdays, December 5 to 26, 2026. Noir Year’s Eve blasts off on Thursday, December 31, 2026. Both shows run 8:00 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.

For more improv, visit the BATS YouTube video channel for free digital clips of BATS Improv’s greatest hits. Online shows from past shows, as well as other BATS Improv reels, are free to view by following Facebook links.

events.title: United Nations Association Film Festival | Opening Night
events.venue: Mitchell Park Community Center 3700 Middlefield Road Palo Alto
events.description:
The 29th United Nations Association Film Festival opens Thursday, Oct. 15, at Mitchell Park Community Center in Palo Alto, with remarks by Mayor Vickie Veenker and the presentation of a City of Palo Alto proclamation recognizing the 29th UNAFF.

Opening Night begins with the West Coast premiere of The Comfort Dogs of Uganda, directed by Australian filmmaker Richard Wainwright. The documentary follows former child soldiers in northern Uganda finding unexpected bonds with rescued village dogs.

Next is the world premiere of Last Christian in Bethlehem, from local Bay Area team and UNAFF alums, Robert Levering, Stephen Talbot, and Stephanie Mechura. This feature documentary provides interviews and footage of Palestinian Christians living in the West Bank.

The night concludes with Through the Body, a film about Keith Terry, an Oakland percussionist and dancer. Director Andrew Reissiger journeys with Terry as he builds a global community through the International Body Music Festival. A special dance performance will also take place at this screening.
https://www.indybay.org/newsitems/2026/10/12/18889270.php

events.title: Green Film Festival of San Francisco
events.address: 4-Star Theater 2200 Clement St San Francisco, CA 94121
events.description:
Oct 15-22, 6pm-11pm

Forget the guilt trip, the Green Film Festival of San Francisco, the mischievous, tree-hugging cousin of the 29 year old SF IndieFest, returns Oct 15-22 to prove that saving the planet doesn't have to feel like homework. We've ditched the doom-and-gloom documentaries that make you want to crawl under a (sustainably sourced) blanket and never come out.

The line-up this year pairs sharp environmental storytelling with wit, weirdness, and unapologetic irreverence. And yes, our Eco-Horror midnight movie is back!

Whether you're an eco-curious cinephile or a die-hard activist, come join in the fun because if we're going to talk about the end of the world as we know it, we might as well laugh, gasp, and maybe even dance a little on the way there.

Through this experience the festival hopes audiences can begin to engage with sustainable solutions to the problems facing the planet.

10-15.

events.title: 20th Street: 51st Annual Potrero Hill Rhythm & Blues Festival
events.address: 20th Street, 20th Street, San Francisco, CA, United States
events.description:
The Potrero Hill R&B Festival will take place Saturday, October 17, 2026 on 20th Street between Wisconsin and Missouri Streets from 10 am – 4 pm. This annual family-friendly festival celebrates the best of our community, featuring local food vendors and artists, live music, historians, homegrown entertainment, and much more. Bring the whole family and join us for this one-of-a-kind community celebration!
Performing on two stages (talent confirmed to date) will be Andre Cruz & Chris Lujan, groove-infused California Soul; and the Curtis Family, the internationally acclaimed family band; Josh Klipp & The Klipptones, a lively jazz and swing band; the JC Smith Blues Band, jumping blues to old school soul; Mitch Woods & His Rocket 88s, modern day boogie-woogie; a youth talent show, and more.
Returning to the festival is the children’s fun fair, promising an exciting experience with mechanical rides, a petting zoo, face painting, a bouncy house, kids crafts, and much more to keep the kids entertained all day.
Festival goers can grab good bites from a variety of food vendors, and the beer and wine garden will be open for everyone 21 and over.
The Festival is a benefit for the two local public elementary schools, Daniel Webster and Starr King, as well as the Potrero Hill Neighborhood House. All donations are tax-deductible.

events.title: United Nations Association Film Festival | Free UNAFF in Schools Program
events.address: Eastside Theater, 1041 Myrtle Street' East Palo Alto
events.description: Category: Festivals / ParadesContact Phone: (650) 724-5544Contact Email: info@unaff.orgCost: FreeLink: https://www.unaff.org/The 29th United Nations Association Film Festival presents UNAFF in Schools, a free program for students and teachers on Wednesday, Oct. 21, in East Palo Alto. The program features two documentaries exploring marine conservation, environmental sustainability and community action.The program opens with Constellations of the Sea, directed and produced by Addie Knoll. The film follows marine biologists in the Maldives as they study and track endangered whale sharks, exploring the relationship between conservation, tourism and the ocean.The program continues with Saving Walden’s World, directed and produced by Jim Merkel, who previously lived in San Luis Obispo. The documentary follows Merkel’s decades-long journey from arms dealer to environmental advocate as he raises his son on an off-the-grid homestead and explores approaches to sustainability around the world.**Admission is free for students and teachers.** This special UNAFF in Schools program offers an opportunity for students and teachers to see two documentaries. The 29th UNAFF runs Oct. 15-25, 2026, with the theme “Passion for Change.” The festival features films addressing human rights issues, including the environment, women’s rights, racism and peace, and engages audiences throughout the Bay Area.

events.description: Category: Festivals / ParadesContact Phone: (650) 724-5544Contact Email: info@unaff.orgCost: 19Link: www.unaff.orgThe 29th United Nations Association Film Festival continues Wednesday, Oct. 21, in San Francisco with an evening of documentaries exploring identity, addiction treatment and institutional accountability.The evening begins with "Becoming James," directed by Evan Possley. The eight-minute documentary follows a man who, after decades in prison, works to rebuild his identity and finds success in an unexpected way.Next is "Shuffle," directed by Benjamin Flaherty. Through the filmmaker’s own recovery, the documentary investigates the multibillion-dollar addiction treatment industry, examining financial incentives, conflicts of interest and the system surrounding people seeking treatment.The evening concludes with "Nuns vs. The Vatican," directed by Lorena Luciano and produced by Filippo Piscopo. The film follows a former Catholic nun who breaks her silence about abuse within the Church, as other nuns come forward to examine a culture of silence and institutional protection.UNAFF runs Oct. 15–25, 2026, with the theme Passion for Change. The festival features films on human rights issues like the environment, women’s rights, racism, and peace, engaging a diverse Bay Area audience.

events.title: Terpnami 2026
events.description:
The highest-level genetics conversation in the world returns to the Bay Area this December to help growers worldwide garden harder, better, faster, and stronger.

Over 1,000 growers big and small from around the world interact with 30 of the world’s top breeders over two days December 5 and 6 in a private Bay Area venue for TERPNAMI. Guests can RSVP today to get ticketing and event details.

The world’s first only ‘seed rave,’ Terpnami runs 12 to 5 p.m. Saturday and Sunday, December 5 and 6, with live DJs, visuals, local food, drink, and creative art and merch collabs; plus pre and after-parties, dinners and meetups.

“Terpnami is the most important seed show in the world,” said California breeder Purple Caper.

Why Terpnami 2026?

California remains the global cannabis epicenter for genetic innovation. Virtually every hot strain in the $60 billion U.S. market, and the global cannabis market beyond, traces its roots to genetics bred or popularized in California. Lemon Cherry Gelato, Z, GSC, OG Kush, and GDP are just few California creations.

Terpnami keeps the Bay Area cannabis genetics beacon lit every December, a time of year when the full-sun harvest seeds are shucked and packaged, and folks are flush with cash for Christmas and thinking about what to grow in 2027.

For year three, Terpnami again shifts to a new venue with historic, theatrical features, crucial mass transit access, and more amenities for guests including off-street parking, and a dedicated restaurant. Our...

events.title: Quinteto Latino
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens covers two square city blocks bounded by Mission, Folsom, Third and Fourth Streets., San Francisco, CA, 94103
events.description:
A wind quintet with an imperative mission, Quinteto Latino is a singular Bay Area-based chamber ensemble devoted to breaking down the racial and social barriers that have long plagued the classical music world. Spotlighting and performing compositions by artists of Latin American heritage, the quintet’s acclaimed musicians are devoted to building community through classical music, performance and advocacy. With concerts featuring expertly melded flute, oboe, clarinet, French horn and bassoon, QL brings out the vibrant colors and vigorous rhythms of Latin American music. The group’s programs include arrangements of beloved Latino folk melodies and contemporary works by illustrious composers such as Gabriela Lena Frank, Orlando Jacinto García and Paquito D’Rivera, including many commissioned by the ensemble.

Supported in part by the Alice M. Ditson Fund of Columbia University.

events.title: El Grupo de Apoyo Latino
events.description:
El Grupo de Apoyo Latino de SFAF es un grupo social y educativo que ofrece un espacio abierto, seguro, y confidencial para apoyar a la comunidad Latina afectada por el VIH y SIDA. Es un grupo diverso, donde el respeto es la base para que todos los asistentes puedan expresar libremente sus experiencias, identidad, étnicidad, nacionalidad, sexualidad, y creencias religiosas.

Todas las reuniones son en español y se llevan a cabo en un ambiente positivo, familiar, y confidencial. Ven a compartir con nosotros, estamos seguros que encontrarás apoyo y recibirás información para mejorar tu calidad de vida.

SFAF ofrece servicios a cualquier persona sin importar su situación migratoria.

Para mas información sobre El Grupo, llama al 415-632-9722.

_____

Our support group, El Grupo, has been a stable source of family and community for Latinos, Latinas and their families since the early 1980s. Join us for information about sexual health and harm reduction, meals and social support, and help finding health and social services.

Meetings are in-person at 940 Howard St Group Room A every Thursday from 3 to 5 pm.

This is Your City. This is Your Voice. This is Your Future. Share your story about growing up and raising your family in San Francisco.

Every family has a story. Every voice matters. Please share yours.

The Women’s Building, 3543 18th Street, SF, CA 94110

Who should attend? Everyone is welcome. This event highlights District 9, but you can attend any Family Summit that fits your schedule.

Why are we gathering? The Family Summit Series is part of San Francisco's first Citywide Community Needs Assessment. Through conversations with families across the city, we're learning what matters most to children, youth, young adults, and families. What we learn will help improve future planning, programs, and services.

Whether you've lived in San Francisco your whole life or recently made it your home, your experiences and ideas matter.

events.title: The History of Concrete
events.description:
Following the finale of his acclaimed HBO series “How To with John Wilson”, NYC documentarian John Wilson looks to the bedrock of his beloved New York City for inspiration and structure. Concrete, the world's most widely used building material, appears as an ever-present life force, and John sets out to make the definitive documentary on the matter. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he decides to use the industry-approved Hallmark formula to tell this seemingly drab story and increase his movie’s appeal. But his foundation soon begins to crumble—literally and figuratively—as he struggles to balance artistic freedom with the realities of the modern film industry.

This film can be used with loyalty cards or our 2026 annual CinemaSFBay passes

events.title: Money in San Francisco politics: Who’s spending big on the election?
events.description:
Wealthy special interests are trying to grab more power in San Francisco — whether they succeed is up to voters.

At
a time when public oversight is shrinking and power is being
concentrated fewer hands, understanding the role of large campaign
donors in our political process has never been more urgent.

Join
Joe Rivano Barros of Mission Local for an in-depth look at who is
spending millions on San Francisco's November 2026 ballot propositions
in an effort to influence your vote. You'll learn how these megadonors
are trying to change the outcome of the election to serve the few, not
the many.

After
Joe's presentation, Lila LaHood of the San Francisco Public Press will
moderate a panel discussion on money in local politics with Darius Kemp
of California Common Cause and Patrick Ford of the San Francisco Ethics
Commission, with time for questions from the audience.

Speakers

Joe Rivano Barros, Executive Editor, Mission Local – Joe is an award-winning journalist whose coverage focuses on
politics, campaign finance, Silicon Valley, and criminal justice. He
received a B.A. at Stanford University for political science in 2014. He
was born in Sweden, grew up in Chile, and moved to Oakland when he was
eight.

events.description:
Aaron Coleman and Jon Cho-Polizzi discuss the challenges and revelations of translating the Black diaspora: examining continuities and ruptures across languages, geographies, and time. The global popularity of Black American culture can provide a reference point across the Black diaspora, but it also serves to obscure local traditions of art and resistance that have developed both independently and in conversation with other diasporic narratives over centuries.

Aaron will discuss his own work as a poet and its influence on his practice in the context of his 2024 translation of Afro-Cuban poet Nicolás Guillén's The Great Zoo, while Jon reflects on the growing visibility of Black and Afro-German art and literature.

About Translator to Translator

Translator to Translator is a translator-curated event series at CAT featuring conversations about the intersections of literature, activism, and identity.

This event series places the Center for the Art of Translation’s (CAT’s) public programming resources directly into the hands of translators, empowering them to curate provocative and timely conversations about language, global literature, and the art of translation. By inviting guest curators to shape our programming, we are creating a space for dream interviews, deep investigations, and fresh perspectives on the work we love.

This series is designed to strengthen our translator community and bring new voices into the discussion. Whether you are a translator, an author, or simp...

In 2016, with the blessing of David Lynch and Angelo Badalamenti, Xiu Xiu released and toured the surprisingly successful album and concert, Plays the Music of Twin Peaks. However, in wanting to always try to follow, honor, and continue to be inspired by the incredibly high bar of artistic challenge set by David Lynch, Xiu Xiu is instead going deeper.

Eraserhead Xiu Xiu is a new live concert with accompanying film & full-length album that uses field recordings, concert specific homemade instruments, organ, modular synths, vocals, flashlights, electrical interference, and elements of musique concrete to express the bizarre emotionality, conflicted sexuality, relentless darkness, and singularly unsettled moonscape of this most incredible of midnight masterpieces. events.description:
Tim Burton had made a name for himself with PEE-WEE'S BIG ADVENTURE, but he really captured everyone's attention with the surprise smash BEETLEJUICE in 1988. The movie was so weird Warner Bros. was almost afraid to spring it on an unsuspecting public. But when they did, audiences went wild for it.

The film also gave substantial boosts to the careers of Alec Baldwin (so young!), Geena Davis, teenage idol Winona Ryder, and of course, Michael Keaton, playing the utterly unpredictable title character. After perishing in a car accident, Barbara (Davis) and Adam (Baldwin) find themselves stuck in their country home, unable to leave as it is invaded by the insufferable Deetze family. When Barbara and Adam are unable to frighten the Deetzes away, they call on the notorious Beetlejuice (Keaton) for help. It's a decision they live (?) to regret.

with Rickie Lee Jones, Wu Fei & Abigail Washburn, Mia Pixley

Creative black tie attire encouraged.

Rickie Lee Jones is an American musician, storyteller, two-time Grammy winner and eight-time nominee who has been inspiring pop culture for decades, beginning with her star-making self-titled debut and the seminal Pirates. Named the “premiere song-stylist and songwriter of her generation” by The New Yorker and “The Duchess of Coolsville” by Time magazine, Jones released her Grammy-nominated album Pieces of Treasure in 2023, a reunion with Russ Titelman, who produced her first two records. events.title: Dead Kennedys
events.description:
Dead Kennedys are an American hardcore punk band formed in San Francisco, California in 1978. The band became part of the American hardcore punk movement of the early 1980s. They gained a large underground fanbase in the international punk rock community, and were one of the first American hardcore bands to make a significant impact in the United Kingdom. Their eclectic music encompassed their trademark loud and fast hardcore, but also spaghetti western, psychedelic, garage rock and rockabilly. Jello Biafra's biting lyrics tackled the sociopolitical concerns of the Reagan era with a distinct sense of morbid humor and satire, following in the footsteps of such earlier rock satirists as Frank Zappa and non-musical countercultural figures like Abbie Hoffman and Lenny Bruce.

In the mid-1980s, the band was embroiled in an obscenity trial in the United States over the artwork of their album Frankenchrist (1985), which included the explicit titular subject of H. R. Giger's Penis Landscape. The band was charged with "distribution of harmful matter to minors", but the trial ended with a hung jury. Dead Kennedys released five studio albums before disbanding in 1986. In 2001, the band reformed without Biafra, who had been in a legal dispute with the remaining members over royalties. The band played three performances in October 2010. At one of the concerts, they debuted their first new song since 1986, "You're Such a Fake".

events.title: YappiScope
events.description:
Dutch avant-garde composer and performance artist Jaap Blonk presents his absurd performance YappiScope. It is Jaap Blonk’s show with visual projections.

It is in ongoing progress, new inventions being added frequently. It contains short videos, scores he wanders through, interactive animations, live soundtracks to silent films and other new multi-media work, with a lot of extended voice work as well as live electronics.

“Blonk’s avant-garde performances channel the provocatively pioneering nonsense of Dadaism. His work is tremendously complex, but his brilliance makes it easy to think the opposite.”

San Francisco Weekly

Jaap Blonk (born 1953 in Woerden, Netherlands) is a self-taught composer, vocalist, poet and visual artist. His unfinished studies in mathematics and musicology created a penchant for activities in a Dada vein, as did several unsuccessful jobs in offices and other well-organised systems.

In the early 1980s he discovered the power and flexibility of his voice, and set out on a long-term research of phonetics and the possibilities of the human voice.

At present, he has developed into a specialist in the creation and performance of sound poetry and a unique vocal improviser, supported by a powerful and uninhibited stage presence. He performs and gives workshops worldwide on a regular basis. With the use of live electronics and projection of visuals the scope and range of his concerts has acquired a considerable extension.

events.description:
Roam x Sirens presents a night in San Francisco marking twenty five years of Roam Recordings, alongside the release of the label's anniversary compilation, 25 Years of Roam. Man Power headlines.

Man Power (Me Me Me / Correspondant, UK) is a producer and DJ from the North East of England, more than a decade deep into a career built on the trust of a scene that doesn't hand that out easily. Labels like DFA, Rekids, and Hivern Discs put his records out because they know he doesn't play safe, and neither does his DJing, and his recent run of collaborations with Juan Maclean under the name Juan Power only sharpens that reputation further. Every set he plays is assembled in the moment, pulled from a mind that jumps between disco, Italo, house, and techno without warning, which means what happens on the night only happens once. There's no replaying it, no catching the same set twice. That's the reason people who've followed him for years still show up early and stay to the end, and why a room that trusts him goes all in the second he steps behind the decks.

He's joined by Shiny Objects (Om Records) and from Roam Recordings: Jason Peters and Chad Mitchell.

San Francisco, CA 94114

RSVP and reserve tickets here

Inspired by Where We Made Room, this workshop sends you out into the Castro for a walking and blind contour drawing session, capturing the buildings and streets that have held queer life for generations. Back at the museum, we'll trace those sketches onto transparency paper to create negatives, then head outside again to turn them into cyanotype prints using sun print paper—letting the sun fix your drawings into deep Prussian blue.

Just as Landeta's silks layer archival exteriors with imagined interiors to blur document and dream, your prints will hold both what's actually there on the block and the loose, intuitive line your hand found along the way.

No drawing experience necessary, all materials provided. Wear shoes ready for a walk.

*Due to the materials cost for this event, GLBT Historical Society Members are limited for one (1) free ticket to this program.

Photo: Jasmine Singh Rosado

Aleo Landeta (they/them) is is a trans and Latine visual artist and educator based in Oakland whose practice spans drawing, painting, installation, and public programming. Their work centers queer joy as liberation, drawing from lived experience and the communities that have held space for them to live authentically. events.description:
Quarry Ampitheater at UC Santa Cruz

Carved from a former limestone quarry in the 1960’s, the historic Quarry Amphitheater located at the heart of the UC Santa Cruz campus reopened after a major renovation in October 2017, welcoming its first ever night time concert with LA based rockers Chicano Batman. With a deep history of hosting legendary artists, activists and authors including Angela Davis, Ravi Shankar, Alfred Hitchcock and Cesar Chavez, the Quarry has reopened as a critical gathering space to celebrate live music and community.

Referred to as the “Red Rocks in the Redwoods”, The Quarry is the largest outdoor venue with an existing stage and seating in the greater Santa Cruz community. The Quarry Amphitheater’s unique terraced asymmetrical design allows for amazing sight-lines and multiple venue configurations from open floor to reserved seating layouts. At a maximum capacity of 2600, The Quarry now holds the opportunity to become the region's premiere outdoor destination concert venue while also retaining its value as a natural open space.

More information: https://www.quarryamphitheater.com

Carved from a former limestone quarry in the 1960’s, the historic Quarry Amphitheater located at the heart of the UC Santa Cruz campus reopened after a major renovation in October 2017, welcoming its first ever night time concert with LA based rockers Chicano Batman. With a deep history of hosting legendary artists, activists and authors including Angela Davis, Ravi Shankar, Alfred Hitchcock and Cesar Chavez, the Quarry has reopened as a critical gathering space to celebrate live music and community.

Referred to as the “Red Rocks in the Redwoods”, The Quarry is the largest outdoor venue with an existing stage and seating in the greater Santa Cruz community. The Quarry Amphitheater’s unique terraced asymmetrical design allows for amazing sight-lines and multiple venue configurations from open floor to reserved seating layouts. At a maximum capacity of 2600, The Quarry now holds the opportunity to become the region's premiere outdoor destination concert venue while also retaining its value as a natural open space.

events.title: Queen Budapest
events.description:
On July 27, 1986, Queen performed the largest-ever stadium concert at the Népstadion in Budapest in front of 80,000 ecstatic fans.

The concert was part of the famed Magic Tour, which was the last time the band toured with lead singer Freddie Mercury. Now, this original concert film has been beautifully rescanned and remastered in 4K alongside a dynamic new audio mix, featuring many of Queen's favorite tracks— "Bohemian Rhapsody,” "Crazy Little Thing Called Love," "I Want To Break Free” and "We Are The Champions."

With three years to go before the fall of the Berlin Wall, this was the first Western rock concert performed in a stadium behind the then Iron Curtain. It was of such significance to the Hungarian authorities and film industry that a group of the country’s top film cameramen and technicians were brought together to film it for posterity.

This film can be used with loyalty cards or our 2026 annual CinemaSF passes

PALACE ARE BACK WITH “KID” AND MASSIVE TOUR OF USA + CANADA

Palace have been making music together for over a decade. What started out as carefree jam sessions between Leo Wyndham, Rupert Turner and Matt Hodges in an airless studio in North London has burgeoned into a project that has amassed a global audience more akin to a community than a fanbase.

Their early EPs - Lost In The Night (2014) and Chase The Light (2015) - were recorded in the band’s beloved aforementioned studio, The Arch, and established a DIY ethos that remains intrinsic to the spirit of the band to this day. Four albums followed; So Long Forever (2016), Life After (2019), Shoals (2022) and Ultrasound (2024): each one a musical exploration of a particular feeling in a particular place during a particular time; ranging from grief and the loss of a relationship to the emergence of new love and light. Consequently, it's not easy to sonically classify Palace. Their sound varies from the atmospheric and ethereal to the more grounded notes of Blues and Americana, yet in every song there is still something remarkably identifiable as Palace: an ineffability to the feelings conjured up...

events.title: Intro to Cyanotype Printing: Sun Prints and Nature Designs on Paper and Fabric
events.description:
- Class Time: 12:00PM - 2:00PM

In this class, we will introduce you to the beautiful art of cyanotype printing! This photographic process is also known as sun printing because the sun can be utilized as the main light source for your exposures. Cyanotype printing is unique in that it allows you to use real life objects, stencils, drawings, and even photo negatives to produce beautiful Prussian blueprints on both artist paper and fabric.

We will lead you through the cyanotype print making process from start to finish, beginning with a discussion of the specific tools and supplies involved, as well as options for prepping your cyanotype solution, paper, and fabric. You will then experiment with exposures by using different objects and image negatives to produce your unique prints. Lastly, you will learn to rinse and dry out your prints, so they are complete and ready to show! You will leave with at least 6-8 prints, including fabric pieces and artist print paper, as well as instructions and know-how to re-create this process at home.

PLEASE NOTE: For evening classes, we'll be using UV lamps rather than the sun to expose your prints. For afternoon classes and events, we'll use a mix of both.

Supplies Needed: None. We supply all ink, paper, and supplies to print. Please wear clothing that can take a hit of ink or two. We will have aprons for you to wear. We encourage you to bring objects from home, such as leaves or small, flat branches. You may bring a photo negative printed...

One of the most derided movies of the 20th century is also one of its most spectacularly misunderstood. The odd-couple tag team of Dutch provocateur director Paul Verhoeven (ROBOCOP, ELLE) and Sleazoid-Hungarian-American writer Joe Eszterhas (FLASHDANCE, SLIVER) first came together with 1992's BASIC INSTINCT, and everyone, including the financial backers and the producer/distributors of this movie, assumed lightning would strike twice for the duo with 1995's SHOWGIRLS. Universally panned by critics upon its initial release, people found the multi-tap combo of inane dialogue, wild over-acting, and extreme obscenity and grotesquerie to be just too much. Then the "so-bad-it's-good" crowd sunk their hollow claws into the movie, claiming it as one of the "best worst" movies of all time. To be sure, yes, this is a movie in which Saved By the Bell's Elizabeth Berkley sets fire to her TV-star image by grinding her pelvis on Kyle MacLachlan's lap until he simulates sexual climax while Gina Gershon watches. She shoves chips into her mouth and reminisces about her days of eating and enjoying "puppy chow," between bouts of trying to make it as a Las Vegas showgirl "goddess."

events.title: 9 to 5
events.description:
Frameline & Another Planet Entertainment present
A Tribute to Dolly Parton
9 to 5
Featuring a drag performance by Peaches Christ

Sunday, October 11 | The Castro

We can’t stay inside a lonely room and cry forever, so dry those tears and join Frameline (a few doors) down at The Castro Theatre for a very special evening celebrating the life, talents, and values of the truly one-of-a-kind Dolly Parton. First, Peaches Christ will pay tribute to the beloved “Jolene” singer with a drag homage, and then we’ll start laughin' and drinkin' and havin' a party with a screening of 9 to 5.

Directed by Colin Higgins (Harold and Maude), this cult classic centers on three women — the exuberant Doralee (Dolly Parton), the timid Judy (Jane Fonda), and the sharp-witted Violet (Lily Tomlin) — as they toil away at Consolidated Companies under the misogynistic Mr. Hart (Dabney Coleman). When talking trash and sharing their wildest revenge fantasies isn’t enough, the trio get even with their bigot of a boss.

Whether you love the film for its titular working-class anthem, its satirical screwball comedy that skewers sexism in the workplace, or the iconic trio at its center, 9 to 5 is undeniably one of the late Dolly Parton’s many great gifts to popular culture.

A percentage of all proceeds from ticket sales will be donated to Dolly Parton’s Imagination Library in honor of its founder.

events.title: PITCH (The Pilot Performance of The Dyke HERstory Dance Tour)
events.description:
As the pilot performance of The Dyke HERstory Dance Tour, PITCH a new, site-specific dance theater project exploring Bay Area queer history through movement, storytelling, and community engagement. Set on the softball field, five dancers embody Bay Area dyke ancestors reuniting as an all-star "ghost team." Each player steps up to bat, sharing her story through recorded audio and embodied movement as the ensemble rounds the bases in a collective portrait of queer community, remembrance, and play. Directed and choreographed by Sarah Bush with research lead by KJ Dahlaw, the work features an original live score by KKINGBOO and B. Dukes of 7000COILS, the Oakland-based, Black-owned, gender-expansive collective.
Created by the multiracial, intergenerational, and queer-led artists of Sarah Bush Dance Project,

PITCH celebrates the enduring legacy of Bay Area lesbian softball as both a cultural touchstone and a place of belonging. The work emerges at a critical moment, as many queer elders who helped build lesbian and dyke communities in Oakland and San Francisco are aging while their stories remain largely absent from public archives and artistic representation. Rather than treating history as something fixed, PITCH invites audiences to experience remembrance as a living, joyful, and embodied act.

Don't miss this extraordinary conversation with Academy Award-winning actor and producer Michael Douglas celebrating the release of his new memoir, One Helluva Ride. A signed bookplate edition of the book is included with each ticket.
Beginning with his fractured childhood and a complex relationship with his superstar father, Kirk Douglas, Michael Douglas finally gives the full and uncensored account of a remarkable life. events.title: All That Heaven Allows
events.description:
This heartbreakingly beautiful indictment of 1950s American mores by Douglas Sirk follows the blossoming love between a well-off widow (Jane Wyman) and her handsome and earthy younger gardener (Rock Hudson). When their romance prompts the scorn of her children and country club friends, she must decide whether to pursue her own happiness or carry on a lonely, hemmed-in existence for the sake of the approval of others. With the help of ace cinematographer Russell Metty, Sirk imbues nearly every shot with a vivid and distinct emotional tenor. A profoundly felt film about class and conformity in small-town America, All That Heaven Allows is a pinnacle of expressionistic Hollywood melodrama.

events.title: Emmet Cohen
events.description:
Miles and Coltrane at 100
Emmet Cohen

Sunday, October 11 | The Freight

Multifaceted American jazz pianist and composer Emmet Cohen has emerged as one of his generation's pivotal figures in music and the related arts. A recognized prodigy, Cohen began Suzuki method piano instruction at age three, and his playing quickly became a mature melding of musicality, technique, and concept. Downbeat observed that his "nimble touch, measured stride and warm harmonic vocabulary indicate he's above any convoluted technical showmanship." In the same spirit, Cohen himself has noted that playing jazz is "about communicating the deepest levels of humanity and individuality; it's essentially about connections," both among musicians and with audiences. He leads his namesake ensemble, the "Emmet Cohen Trio," is a vibrant solo performer, and is in constant demand as a sideman. Possessing a fluid technique, an innovative tonal palette, and an extensive repertoire, Cohen plays with the command of a seasoned veteran and the passion of an artist fully devoted to his medium.

In celebration of the centennial of John Coltrane and Miles Davis, pianist Emmet Cohen brings together an all-star quintet to explore the fundamental questions that shaped their artistry: Why are we here? What are we reaching for? Where does the music take us?

A dynamic ensemble led by pianist Emmet Cohen, featuring saxophonist Tivon Pennicott and Trumpeter Jeremy Pelt will celebrate these geniuses in Miles and Coltrane at 100...

events.title: Air Supply
events.description:
A Matter of Time Tour
Air Supply

Sunday, October 11 | The Mountain Winery

Graham Russell & Russell Hitchcock met on May 12, 1975, the first day of rehearsals for "Jesus Christ Superstar" in Sydney, Australia; they became instant friends with their common love for The Beatles and, of course, singing.

After the shows' performances at 10:30, they would play pizza parlors, coffee bars and night clubs with just one guitar and two voices. They quickly gained a reputation for great harmonies and for original songs that Graham was constantly writing. They made a demo on a cassette of two songs, "Love and Other Bruises" and "If You Knew Me" and took it to every record company in Sydney. Everyone turned it down but one — CBS Records — who admired their unique style.

They made a single in one afternoon and it shot to number one on the national charts. Air Supply was born! That same year, they opened for Rod Stewart across Australia and then throughout the U.S. and Canada playing all of the famous huge venues before Rod would take the stage. They found new fans, but did not break the U.S. market.

Back in Australia they had to start again and made a record called Life Support. On this record were some treasures of songs, including "Lost in Love" which went Top 10 in Australia and somehow found its way to music industry executive Clive Davis in New York.

Clive immediately signed Air Supply to Arista Records and in 1980, "Lost in Love" became the fastest selling single in the world, l...

events.title: Repo! The Genetic Opera
events.description: In the year 2056 – the not-so-distant future – an epidemic of organ failures devastates the planet. Out of the tragedy, a savior emerges: GeneCo, a biotech company that offers organ transplants, for a price. Those who miss their payments are scheduled for repossession and hunted by villainous Repo Men. In a world where surgery addicts are hooked on painkilling drugs and murder is sanctioned by law, a sheltered young girl searches for the cure to her own rare disease as well as information about her family's mysterious history. After being sucked into the haunting world of GeneCo, she is unable to turn back, as all of her questions will be answered at the wildly anticipated spectacular event: The Genetic Opera. The film features a goth rock/opera score sung by genre favorites Paul Sorvino, Anthony Stewart Head, Sarah Brightman, and Bill Moseley.

events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens covers two square city blocks bounded by Mission, Folsom, Third and Fourth Streets., San Francisco, CA, 94103

Join us in celebration of San Francisco Indigenous Peoples Day with a magnificent profusion of Native American art, music and vendors. The event highlights the vastly diverse and talented community of Indigenous artists in the Bay Area, California and the Americas. Presented on Yelamu, Ramaytush Ohlone Territory, in partnership with the International Indian Treaty Council, the program at Yerba Buena Gardens follows the Annual Indigenous Peoples Day Sunrise Gathering on Alcatraz – please check the IITC website for updates. Schedule to be announced.

A groundbreaking Indigenous musician whose art flows directly out of his cultural activism, tenor Jeremy Dutcher is a conservatory-trained Canadian composer, musicologist and performer who has turned European classical music into a vehicle for language preservation. A member of Neqotkuk First Nation in Eastern Canada now based in Montréal, Québec, Dutcher catapulted to renown with his debut album Wolastoqiyik Lintuwakonawa, which won the 2018 Polaris Music Prize and the Juno Award for Indigenous Music Album of the Year at the Canadian equivalent of the Grammys in 2019. The project unearthed century-old archival recordings of his ancestors, which he turned into collaborative compositions on piano. Sung entirely in Wolastoqey, his endangered mother tongue, the album led to collaborations with artists such as Yo-Yo Ma and Feist. events.title: Naza
events.description:
NAZA screens at NEW PEOPLE October 9–11 before moving to The Roxie starting October 12.

In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them.

Directors Note:

We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanisation of another?

What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

– Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

events.title: Bea Arthur: The Documentary
events.description:
Co-presented by Frameline

The Bay Area premiere of a new documentary offering an intimate look at the life and career of Emmy and Tony Award–winning performer Bea Arthur.

The film is built around a never‑before‑seen interview with Arthur, paired with new conversations from colleagues and friends who worked alongside her throughout her remarkable career. From her early days at The New School, to her groundbreaking work in off‑Broadway, Broadway, cabaret, and television, the documentary traces Arthur’s evolution into one of entertainment’s most distinctive voices.

Audiences will revisit her iconic roles as Maude and Dorothy Zbornak on The Golden Girls, her Tony‑winning turn as Vera Charles in Mame, and her decades‑long advocacy for the LGBTQ+ community. The film reveals the Bea Arthur few ever saw: sharp, compassionate, fiercely intelligent, and deeply committed to the causes she championed.

A post screening conversation with filmmaker and producer Dan Watt in person.

events.title: The Texas Chain Saw Massacre (1974)
events.description: Nothing will ever diminish the power of THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE. Shot through a cinéma vérité lens, director Tobe Hooper's ferocious classic follows five friends that fall victim to the grotesque Leatherface and his cannibalistic family. With a beautifully raw DIY aesthetic and powerful performances, this shockingly realistic film revolutionized the horror landscape when it was unleashed on a politically and socially tumultuous America in 1974. Facing controversy and censorship throughout its troubled release, THE TEXAS CHAIN SAW MASSACRE has stood the test of time to become a landmark film and cultural milestone.

What would you give for a chance to be the most omnipotent version of yourself? To finally be rid of the petty human desires that keep you from achieving greatness? To finally have it all, everything you’ve ever wanted? What would you trade? What are you willing to lose? What would you do for power?

These questions are at the core of KiNG MALA’s debut album, And You Who Drowned In The Grief Of A Golden Thing. Across its wide-ranging 12 tracks – which seesaw between invigorating industrial pop and delicately refined R&B balladry – the singer-songwriter spins a tale as equally rooted in a sci-fi nightmare as it is in reality.

The album follows the classic storyline of a hero’s journey to redemption, focusing on two non-descript, fictionalized characters: a human and an all-mighty entity. The front half is packed with the wonder of “what if.” What would an exchange for power look like? And more importantly, what would it sound like? (Think the experimental, living aesthetic of Bon Iver’s 22, A Million or Dijon's Absolutely, she offers – but with more bite.)

The back half of the project provides answers – and it’s not pretty. By the story’s end, the human not only lacks power, but everything that made then human as well. “It's what we become, because the real dark shit that happens to women, you are never the same,” KiNG Mala shares.

And at a time when the world is embracing such left-of-center storytelli...

events.title: Swimming Home — Documentary World Premiere + Q&A
events.description:
A feature documentary about one man's solo swim across the English Channel — and the promise to his mother that drove it.

100% of ticket sales go to cancer research at Gustave Roussy, Europe's leading cancer research and treatment centre, in France.

Swimming Home is a feature documentary about one man's attempt to swim the English Channel — solo, without a wetsuit, across 21 miles of cold, unpredictable water known as the "Everest of swims."

The film follows Erwan Le Roy, a French-born San Franciscan with no endurance-swimming background, over the year he spends transforming himself, body and mind, for a crossing most people would never attempt. What starts as a promise to his mother after her cancer diagnosis becomes a true story about grief, hope, and what it takes to keep going when every reason to quit is right there in the water.

World Premiere, followed by a live Q&A with Erwan Le Roy, the swimmer at the center of the film.

events.description:
NAZA screens at NEW PEOPLE October 9–11 before moving to The Roxie starting October 12.

In secret conversations on the rooftops of Tel Aviv at night, the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza are revealed by the people who designed and operated them.

Directors Note:

We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanisation of another?

What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

– Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor

Join Yotam Ottolenghi for an intimate and energizing evening celebrating his forthcoming Fall 2026 cookbook, Simple Too, the long-awaited follow-up to his bestselling Ottolenghi Simple. Eight years after redefining “flavor without fuss,” Ottolenghi returns to explore what “simple” means now — in a world of endless notifications, long commutes, and minds split between podcasts, WhatsApp groups, and homework help.
In conversation, he’ll share how Simple Too was born from real life: recipes that work with you, not against you — dishes you can begin with half a plan and still end with a deeply satisfying meal. Expect laughter, honesty, and that signature Ottolenghi spark as he declares, “The lemon is back!” and explains why bold flavor remains at the heart of simplicity.

Drawing from the book’s vibrant themes, Ottolenghi will dive into the ingredients and techniques that quietly shape this new collection: beans simply dressed, black chickpeas, sesame in generous handfuls, sweet- and-spicy balances, pasta cooked directly in its sauce, and whole meals roasted start-to-finish in a single tray (with far less washing up). He’ll also introduce the new “Fundamentals” chapter — fifteen fridge-ready flavor builders like spring onion oil, green salsa, za’atar oil, confit tomatoes, and chilli crisp — the small things that make big differences on the busiest weeknights. They will quickly become your new creative obsession as you experiment with getting different houseplants, succulents, and even herbs into the kokedama bonsai mix!

In this class, you will learn how to assemble your kokedama plant and moss ball using string to bind it together. You will take a crack at constructing two kokedama moss ball projects (one small and one medium). You’ll receive instruction on proper plant care as well as recommendations on which “hard to kill” houseplants and succulents to use so that your kokedama creations are guaranteed a long and happy life! You will leave with two kokedama moss balls of your making, as well as a plant care guide and supplies list so that you can keep adding on to your hanging kokedama plants at home!

Supplies Needed: None. We will supply all plants, string, moss, and other materials for your kokedama projects.

The Talk

How Science Can Improve Health for Women … and Men

The Speaker
Holly A. Ingraham, PhD, is the Herzstein Professor of Molecular Physiology at the University of California, San Francisco. Her research focuses on hormone-responsive nodes in the brain and peripheral tissues that impact metabolic, skeletal, and gut physiology and women’s health. Through question-driven basic science, Ingraham has uncovered how hormonal fluctuations lead to adaptive responses in females across their lifespan. Ingraham is an elected fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science and a member of the National Academy of Sciences and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. She earned her Ph.D. from UCSD.

Director Mohammed Ali Naqvi on site for a post-screening Q&A.

On the morning of August 22, 2023, eight passengers – six of them schoolboys – board a makeshift cable car for what should be a routine commute to school in the mountains of northern Pakistan. Midway across a deep ravine, two of the three supporting cables snap. The gondola lurches violently and comes to rest, suspended more than 900 feet above the ground by a singled amaged wire.

What follows unfolds in realtime over the course of one harrowing day – a survival ordeal shaped by uncertainty, escalating danger, and the relentless pressure of being watched. The rescue plays out live on national television and social media, captured from every angle: panicked families on the ground, military helicopters battling high winds, first responders scrambling for solutions, drones circling overhead, and footage filmed from inside the cablecar itself as hours pass and darkness approaches.

With no margin for error and a cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of rescuers must improvise under intense public scrutiny – racing against an invisible clock before disaster strikes live on television.

“…provides a dash of thrill, magnifying the events of this human interest story to cinematic scope, and giving audiences a sense of the chaos, the tension, and the catharsis of that tumultuous day of terror…” – Jason Gorber, povmagazine.com

events.address: 988 Market St., 9th Fl, San Francisco, CA, 94102
events.description:
Join Tiny News Collective for a conversation with the community-centered founders rebuilding and reimagining local news.

From the Ground Up: The Founders Reimagining Local News
You already know one story about local news: outlets shrinking and closing, and chains buying up what remains.
But across the country, and here in San Francisco, a different story is being written. Founders are building small, independent newsrooms in the places they live, accountable to their neighbors. A form of community infrastructure, built on trust: tiny news.
Join us for a panel with Tiny News Collective executive director Amy Kovac-Ashley, COYOTE Media Collective co-founder Soleil Ho, News Relay Network co-founder Daphne Magnawa, and News Futures lead steward Darryl Holliday. They'll discuss new research on what it takes for tiny newsrooms to launch and last, and why these types of newsrooms are critical for the future of journalism and democracy.

A dating event for those who are fed up w apps + are ready for a more embodied approach.

// about \\

‘the feels’ is a 3-hour in-person dating event in SF, designed for people who understand that dating is a skill we need to practice, to maintain our relational health.

Part somatic experience, part mindful singles event, part human connection experiment — ‘the feels ‘offers a different way to date: slower, tuned into your body, and rooted in emotional awareness.

Created by Allie Hoffman as part of her masters degree thesis work at Columbia University’s Spirit Mind Body Institute, ‘the feels’ blends Jungian psychology, somatic intelligence, mindfulness, and authentic relating into one immersive evening.

The format builds off the work of Carl Jung, Joseph Campbell, Dr Martha Eddy, the Buddha + the Tavistock Institute - among others.

‘The feels’ level 1 experience guides you through 4 structured pairings and group moments that include deep prompts, positive reflections, and somatic elements like eye gazes + hugs.

For Finn Wolfhard, music has long existed as something instinctual. An outlet he’s returned to at every stage of his life, whether as a form of escape, expression, or something different entirely. His 2025 solo debut Happy Birthday captured that impulse in its rawest form, introducing a deeply personal songwriting voice. But with his forthcoming 2026 album, Fire From The Hip, Wolfhard shifts the lens, offering something broader in scope, yet just as personal in feeling.

“When I was on tour for my last album, I had such an amazing time playing with my friends who are also my backing band. After the last tour, I started writing new songs and knew I wanted them to capture the same energy of our live shows, the chemistry and the dynamic of our friendship, which ultimately became the inspiration behind the new album” Wolfhard says.

While the new record builds on thematic threads from Happy Birthday —nostalgia, uncertainty, the turbulence of growing up—it approaches them from different vantage points. Written during a period of transition, including a move back to Vancouver, the songs reflect an artist taking stock of where he’s been and who he’s becoming. As Wolfhard puts it, “Nostalgia is a big factor for me when writing and in my life. To me, music is something that’s universal and can be shared with each other. On the afternoon of his first appearance onstage with the Sex Pistols, last summer at Bush Hall, Frank Carter’s peaceful afternoon stroll on the streets of Shepherd’s Bush was interrupted by a stranger sat outside a pub. “Big shoes,” the man shouted; nothing more, nothing less.

“That’s all he said,” Carter reports. “And I just replied ‘thanks for noticing’, and off I walked. But I thought, ‘Fucking hell, we’ve not even played one note yet’. At that point I felt like I was melting. I realised I had to get my shit together here.”

As if the matter was ever in doubt, hours later, he did just that. The stranger’s assertion that anyone stepping up to the microphone with the band who terrorised a nation faces one of the tallest orders in rock and roll – make no mistake, filling big shoes requires big cojones – overlooked the fact that he was speaking to one of the few singers, and perhaps even the <> singer, capable of handling the job. events.title: The Tenses + MSHR + Sung Kim
events.description:
Buy Tickets

Doors 8pm / Show 8:30pm

$17 / free or discounted for members

The Tenses—comprised of Ju Suk Reet Meate and Oblivia from Smegma, the legendary “band without musicians” founded in 1973—held a tradition of weekly jam sessions with MSHR (Brenna Murphy & Birch Cooper) beginning in 2012. The jam room AKA “Smegma Studios” AKA “purple planet room,” was a longtime anchor of the Portland underground music scene with a rotating cast of weirdos and noise musicians coming through over the decades. Lifelong archivists, The Tenses would record and catalog every session, occasionally releasing highlights on labels such as their own Pigface Records, including a collaborative release with MSHR in 2015.

The two duos converge for a rare west coast tour, with The Tenses’ collection of cassette recorders, plastic water jugs, pocket trumpet, Ciat-Lonbarde synths, and occasional surf rock riffs. MSHR’s new work, Negative Flower, combines their signature physical controllers and light feedback with a digital system constructed in the SuperCollider programming environment. Sung Kim joins for an opening set with his expertly crafted handmade musical constructions drawing on kotos, lap steel, and various other stringed instruments.

The vision for this convening is to amplify and uplift the 2027 Emerging Women of Color LeadStrong Cohort’s learnings and collective power-building strategies. events.description:
What happens when two chefs from very different culinary traditions meet around a shared fascination with cooking over fire?
For one night only, Chef Earth (Saritwat Wanvichitkun) and Pastry Chef Pond (Chayanin Tanapradit) of Bangkok’s Saawaan are coming to Lake Tahoe for a special collaboration with Chef Koji Hanada and Pastry Chef/Culinary Director Matt Tinder of Smoke Door Lake Tahoe.
Saawaan is one of Bangkok’s acclaimed contemporary Thai restaurants, having held a Michelin star for four consecutive years. Its tasting menu explores regional Thai flavors through techniques including fermenting, steaming, boiling and charcoal grilling. Chef Earth, a Phuket native trained in both French and Thai cooking, leads the savory kitchen, while Chef Pond brings a pastry approach that combines classical technique with Thai ingredients and flavors.
Recently, Earth has become increasingly interested in wood-fire cooking and the possibilities it opens up, making Smoke Door - and its fire-driven kitchen in the mountains - a particularly interesting place for this collaboration.
Rather than creating a conventional fusion menu, the chefs will cook side by side across eight courses, alternating between Saawaan and Smoke Door. The dinner becomes a conversation between two distinct perspectives: Earth’s modern interpretation of Thai cuisine and Koji’s contemporary Japanese cooking, connected by a shared curiosity about fire.

events.title: United Nations Association Film Festival | Opening Night
events.description:
The 29th United Nations Association Film Festival opens Thursday, Oct. 15, at Mitchell Park Community Center in Palo Alto, with remarks by Mayor Vickie Veenker and the presentation of a City of Palo Alto proclamation recognizing the 29th UNAFF.

Opening Night begins with the West Coast premiere of The Comfort Dogs of Uganda, directed by Australian filmmaker Richard Wainwright. The documentary follows former child soldiers in northern Uganda finding unexpected bonds with rescued village dogs.

Next is the world premiere of Last Christian in Bethlehem, from local Bay Area team and UNAFF alums, Robert Levering, Stephen Talbot, and Stephanie Mechura. This feature documentary provides interviews and footage of Palestinian Christians living in the West Bank.

The night concludes with Through the Body, a film about Keith Terry, an Oakland percussionist and dancer. Director Andrew Reissiger journeys with Terry as he builds a global community through the International Body Music Festival. A special dance performance will also take place at this screening.

events.title: LITQUAKE: A 22nd-Century Conservation Ethos for California
events.description:
ogether, let's imagine a new conservation ethos—one rooted in restoration, resilience, and reciprocity

FREE, $10-$15 suggested donation

Sponsored by Heyday Books
Co-presented with LITQUAKE

California’s landscapes have long been shaped by deep relationships between people and place. But that relationship has changed dramatically over time, especially with the rise of European American settlement and the erasure of Traditional Ecological Knowledge.

Panelists Obi Kaufmann, creator of the California Field Atlas series; Laura Cunningham, award-winning author of A State of Change; and earth scientist and professional mountain biker Dillon Osleger examine how modern society has grown increasingly estranged from the natural world. Together, they imagine a new conservation ethos—one rooted in restoration, resilience, and reciprocity—and ask what it would take for Californians to leave the state healthier, more biodiverse, and more ecologically whole at the end of the 21st century than at its beginning. Moderated by Leslie Carol Roberts. Doors at 6:30pm.

We'll cover when and how to cut back and prune thoughtfully, leaving seed heads, hollow stems, and leaf litter in place where they matter most, so overwintering insects and beneficial pollinators have the habitat they need. You'll leave with a practical framework for fall garden cleanup that works with nature's cycles rather than against them, plus techniques you can apply right away in your own garden.

Whether you're new to pollinator-friendly gardening or looking to refine your seasonal routine, this session offers guidance you can put into practice this fall.

“I’ve always wanted to use that title,” Sam Beam says of Hen’s Teeth, his eighth full-length album and his sixth for Sub Pop Records. “I just love it. To me it suggests the impossible. Hen’s teeth do not exist. And that’s what this record felt like: a gift that shouldn’t be there but it is. An impossible thing but it’s real.”

Hen’s Teeth and his previous album, Light Verse, are siblings of a sort. They were recorded during the same sessions after a years-long dry spell, with the same band, at Waystation studio in Laurel Canyon. “When I’ve been on a writing kick, and the band can meet me where I’m at, they push me into something I hadn’t imagined. I’m at a point in my life where spontaneity is a lot more important to me. I don’t have as much to prove as I used to. I’m a lot freer and I love making music more than ever. There are no right or wrong answers. You just pray for your luck and try your best.”

In this case prayers were answered and luck struck hard. The musicians cohered so quickly and inspired each other so much that they were often getting songs recorded in just a few takes, sometimes at the rate of two or three per day. The two albums might therefore be thought of as fraternal twins: they share DNA and complement each other but have distinct identities and are defined as much by their differences as their similarities.

events.title: Here-ish & Queer-ish: Stories of Queer Jewish California
events.venue: Jewish Community Center of San Francisco
events.description:
Join the JCCSF, Keshet, Nice Jewish Boys+, and Sapphic Jewish Social Club for a joyful evening of creativity, and connection. Come for Shabbat, stay for stories, laughter, and live performances celebrating Queer Jewish life right here in California.
For generations, California, and the Bay Area especially, has been a place to land when you needed somewhere to seek refuge, find your people, reinvent yourself, and build something entirely your own. Together, we’ll explore that legacy and what it really means to find Queer Jewish belonging here today.
We’ll welcome Shabbat with candles glowing, wine poured, and challah shared, before settling in for featured performers and then opening the mic to you. Poetry, music, comedy, a story that’s been sitting in your heart for years, whatever you’ve got, we want to hear it. Or come as you are, grab a chair, and just listen.
Whether you come to perform, meet new people, celebrate Shabbat, or simply experience a night of Queer Jewish joy, there’s a place for you here.
Interested in taking the mic?
After you register, keep an eye out for your confirmation email, it’ll include a form where you can sign up to perform at the open mic. We’ll follow up to confirm participation!
Questions about the open mic? Email Lorenn Kassel, JCCSF Public Programs Manager at lkassel@jccsf.org.
What to Expect
Shabbat rituals to welcome the evening
Featured performances and a community open mic
Nosh and drinks

events.title: San Franpsycho X Dirtybird 25 Years Of Psycho Closing Party
events.description:
Get ready to dance all night and celebrate 25 wild years of psycho vibes with San Franpsycho and Dirtybird!

This is your last chance to dive into 25 wild years of Psycho with San Franpsycho's epic retrospective, live and in person. Before the show comes down for good, two homegrown SF institutions are joining forces to throw one hell of a send-off.
Some brands make clothes. SFP made a culture out of Ocean Beach, a striped van, and a city that claimed it as its own. "Quarter Century of Psycho: A San Franpsycho Retrospective" puts 25 years of that story in one room. It brings together work from local artists, original shirts, art, posters, archival footage, collabs, and real stories from the people whose lives SFP touched along the way. It's a look back, and a nod to everything it took to get here.
The centerpiece of the night is a screening of the second San Franpsycho surf film, "Wet and Wreckless," which hasn't been seen publicly in over two decades.
Then, the flock takes over. Dirtybird has been dropping basslines and spreading good times from San Francisco to dancefloors around the world since it started with parties in Golden Gate Park. For the closing night, two Dirtybird DJs will take the decks, and their names are staying under wraps until closer to the party. Follow @sanfranpsycho and @dirtybird so you're first to know when the lineup drops. Expect bass-heavy, booty-shaking house, plenty of mischief, and a room full of the people who made both brands what they are.

events.title: FOSS: an immersive live audiovisual experience
events.description:
FOSS is an immersive live audiovisual experience where electronic music, cinematic visuals, and cutting-edge technology converge. Created by Grammy-nominated pianist and composer Romain Collin and producer/electronic musician Jeremy Loucas, the performance grew from Collin’s six-month artistic retreat in the remote Icelandic highlands, where silence, vast landscapes, and isolation inspired a striking new creative vision.

Performed entirely live using modular synthesizers, tape machines, keyboards, and custom analog instruments—with no pre-recorded tracks—FOSS surrounds audiences with richly layered ambient soundscapes, projection-mapped visuals, and a quadraphonic sound system. The result is a mesmerizing, genre-defying performance that blurs the boundaries between music, film, nature, and technology.

Learn more at fossfossfoss.com

events.title: Gummo
events.description:
Harmony Korine’s debut feature is an audacious, lyrical evocation of America’s rural underbelly, and an elegy in the southern-gothic tradition of William Faulkner and William Eggleston. Shot in Korine’s native Nashville—standing in for the tornado-ravaged Xenia, Ohio—the rough-hewn film follows two young friends, Tummler and Solomon, as they ride around town, huffing glue and hunting stray cats, their every local encounter charged with vaudevillian anarchy as well as deep pathos. At once transgressive and empathetic, disturbing and undeniably beautiful, Gummo is a one-of-a-kind portrait of angelic and devilish souls caught in a cultural void, circumscribed by poverty and the depleted, alienated spiritual life of late-twentieth-century America.

This film can be used with loyalty cards or our 2026 annual CinemaSFBay passes

events.description:
As a girl growing up in the 90s, everyone seemed to know Rebecca had Autism Spectrum Disorder except for her! And her parents! However, one thing was crystal clear: she had no idea how to “act normal.” This show will cover Rebecca's hilarious journey of self-exploration and her lifelong struggle to adapt, including at one point literally googling “how to act normal” and landing on the pinnacle of the ‘00s internet: WikiHow.
ABOUT REBECCA
Rebecca Kaplan is an adorably awkward standup comedian. Her acerbic wit and relatable insights have entertained crowds all over the world. She's appeared on the Late Show with David Letterman and has been featured on SiriusXM, NPR, and the front page of WorldStarHipHop. She lives in NYC, where she co-hosts the Bad Fan Fic podcast. Follow her on all social media at @RebeccaTKaplan to check out her clips.

events.title: Froggy’s 30th Birthday Featuring Corey Kent with Max Vogel
events.venue: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
events.address: 50 Mark West Springs Road, Santa Rosa, CA, 95403
events.description:
Froggy 92.9 celebrates its 30th birthday with a high-energy country celebration featuring Sony Music Nashville’s Corey Kent. Kent brings his signature blend of Oklahoma grit, country soul and rebel rock energy to the stage for a performance built on conviction, powerhouse vocals and hard-earned momentum. Rising from the dancehalls and dive bars of Bixby, Oklahoma, Kent has carved his own lane in country music with a sound influenced by Bruce Springsteen and Creedence Clearwater Revival as much as George Strait and Brooks & Dunn. His journey has been defined by perseverance, from early Nashville setbacks to a breakout run that now includes two No. 1 country radio hits, the 3X Platinum “Wild As Her,” the Gold-certified “This Heart,” Platinum-certified “Something’s Gonna Kill Me” and more than one billion career streams. With his latest album, Heartland Rock and Roll, Kent leans fully into the sound that sets him apart: smoky vocals, small-town storytelling, country-rock intensity and a deep sense of gratitude earned through the slow build.

Opening the celebration is Max Vogel, a Windsor-based country artist known for honest storytelling, strong melodies and a modern take on traditional country roots. Together, Corey Kent and Max Vogel deliver a spirited night of music that blends national country star power with local Sonoma County energy. Join us in celebrating Froggy’s 30th birthday with a concert you won’t want to miss!

events.title: An Evening with Mike Kuchar
events.description:
The vibrant, poetic and wild works of Mike Kuchar have inspired generations of filmmakers and artists with their wickedly perverse parodies of pop-culture and abundant creativity. From early 8 mm films made with his twin brother George Kuchar featuring friends from their Bronx neighbourhood to the underground sci-fi extravaganza Sins of the Fleshapoids 1965, his films take the language of Hollywood and make it so ‘overblown it’s glorious’. In the 1990s Mike Kuchar embraced video with the same transformative passion that he brought to his early 8 mm films, and created a vast body of work ranging from delirious teleplays to recent digital fantasies, displaying a unique creative sensibility. Relishing the possibilities of the most minuscule budgets his films are radiant and lurid in equal measure, celebrating human creativity with an undiminished passion and humor for over 50 years.

Program:

Age of Awareness: A mind blowing journey into the New Age

Forward Fancies: Unbridled poets recites audacious poems

events.description:
Buy Tickets

$27 adv / $29 door / free or discounted for members

Member tickets are not yet available for Fall 2026 Programs

Marisa Anderson's music transcends borders. The topography of her work interrogates the intersections of artistry and expression with form and tradition. A singular guitarist and voracious musical collaborator, Anderson crafts pieces bursting with equal parts reverence and curiosity, contouring familiar shapes into work that is wholly her own.

The Anthology of UnAmerican Folk Music is a collection of nearly one thousand songs culled from the private record collection of the late Harry Smith. Assembled by Anderson after a chance encounter led to an opportunity to study and explore this treasure trove of music, the Anthology focuses on music from places that the United States has been in conflict with since 1970: Southeast Asia, the USSR and the Arabic and Islamic regions of the world. In Volume 1 Anderson presents her own deeply personal iterations of nine songs from the Anthology. Composed, transcribed and arranged through a process of trial and error, deep listening and research, Anderson charts a musical course from Afghanistan to Vietnam via Yemen, Cambodia and Turkmenistan.

events.title: The Power of Loving Awareness
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Mark Coleman
Mindfulness and love are essential and beautiful qualities of an awakened life. Mindfulness leads to clarity, insight, and understanding while compassion is an attitude of heart that cares deeply about life’s challenges. Combined, they allow a kind embrace of the pain and struggles that arise in ourselves, each other, and the world.
During this heartfelt day of meditation, we will discover how these qualities are essential in responding to the inevitable stresses and suffering that are part of being human. We will explore how they are necessary in any journey of awakening and in learning to live wisely and kindly in the midst of difficulty.
Participants will cultivate awareness through mindfulness meditations, and develop a compassionate orientation through heart-opening practices. Teachings will focus on the integration of love and awareness as a response to suffering and pain. We will also inquire into what obstructs the natural expression of the heart.

events.title: The Art of Succulent Terrariums: A Hands-On Workshop
events.description:
Imagine having your very own little world that's exactly how you want it to be. A tiny pocket dimension you can escape to when life gets stressful or you just need a dose of zen. Your very own ecosystem, created with your own two hands. No, this isn't some creator god fantasy. It's our Terrarium Workshop.

Speaking from experience, having some greenery around the house definitely boosts my mood, and taking care of it is its own kind of satisfaction. A terrarium is that feeling, but twice over. It's a tiny plant oasis that you get to design however you like and then tend to like some sort of benevolent domestic plant deity.

What's even cooler is that terrariums exist because of a happy accident that helped shape the modern world.
In 1829, a London physician named Nathaniel Bagshaw Ward sealed a moth chrysalis inside a glass bottle and accidentally changed the way plants traveled around the world. His little experiment led to the invention of the Wardian case, a glass container that helped smuggle tea out of China, launch the global rubber trade (historically important, even if that part didn't exactly age well), and eventually bring the Cavendish banana to grocery stores everywhere.

Fast forward a couple hundred years, and we're using the same basic idea for something a little less world-changing, but arguably more fun. In this workshop, you'll build a thriving little desert in glass that can happily live on your windowsill for years with very little effort.
