it’s murph is a Nashville-based electronic producer crafting dance music that’s meant to be felt as much as it’s heard. Rooted in emotion but built for movement, his sound lives at the intersection of euphoric melody, gritty low-end, and expansive atmosphere — pulling listeners into moments that feel both intimate and anthemic.

Driven by the belief that music is a multi-sensory experience, it’s murph creates records designed to unlock something deeper: a memory, a feeling, a shared release on the dancefloor. His productions balance warmth and edge, pairing melodic progressions with driving grooves that keep crowds locked in while leaving space to breathe.

Blending influences from tech house, bass-forward dance, and melodic electronic music, his sound draws inspiration from artists like Fred again.., Cloonee, and Chris Lake, while remaining distinctly his own. Whether in headphones or under strobe lights, it’s murph’s music invites listeners to step outside themselves and fully immerse in the moment.

As his catalog continues to grow, it’s murph is carving out a lane defined by emotional energy, forward-thinking production, and a deep connection to the people on the other side of the speakers.

Merry Mozart
events.description:
Journey to a place where personal expression and timeless beauty meet in radiant harmony as three composers reveal their most poetic and expressive selves.

Written as a birthday gift for his wife and first performed on Christmas morning, Richard Wagner’s Siegfried Idyll is a rare glimpse of the gentler side of the composer. Filled with tenderness and intimacy, the work is an idyllic unfolding of glowing harmonies, pastoral, calm, and deeply personal affection.

Ottorino Respighi’s Trittico Botticelliano brings three Renaissance paintings to vivid musical life. Inspired by Botticelli’s La Primavera, The Adoration of the Magi, and The Birth of Venus, Respighi’s orchestration shimmers with color and imagination, transforming visual beauty into sound that is refined, atmospheric, and richly evocative.

Mozart’s Symphony No. 39 is a work of noble warmth and exuberant invention. Majestic yet playful, the symphony balances ceremonial grandeur with lyric elegance, offering music that sparkles with clarity, wit, and humanity.

Dagmar Zuniga

Nicaraguan-American artist Dagmar Zuniga makes music that feels both intimate and expansive: songs drift like disrupted signals, carried by harmony, tape hiss, and a strong sense of touch. Her debut solo album in filth your mystery is kingdom / far smile peasant in yellow music — written and recorded in New York, Norway, and Athens, Georgia over a period of five years on her longtime companion, the Tascam 424 — was released by the People’s Coalition of Tandy on Bandcamp & YouTube in January 2025, accompanied by a small tape run that sold out instantly. The project quickly garnered over two hundred thousand views and the attention of artists such as Mount Eerie, who invited her to tour with them that summer.

This year, what was once a jewel of tapped-in algorithms and message boards will meet the world at large, with in filth arriving digitally on March 4, and physically on April 10, via AD 93.

in filth is an atmospheric, devotional collage where one voice multiplies into a chorus of selves, sometimes delicate, sometimes severe; an effect created by Zuniga’s masterful layering of texture and complex harmonies. Synths glitter out like spears of sunlight from beneath clouds of moody, time-distorted guitars, and songs spin about themselves like tightly-wound music boxes, making use of a kind of hypnotic repetition, before melting apart into their components or slipping into the following track.

events.description:
Circle Jerks (stylized as Ciʀcle JƎʀᴋs) are an American hardcore punk band, formed in 1979 in Los Angeles, California. The group was founded by former Black Flag vocalist Keith Morris and Redd Kross guitarist Greg Hetson. To date, Circle Jerks have released six studio albums, one compilation, a live album and a live DVD. Their debut album, Group Sex (1980), is considered a landmark of the hardcore genre.

The band has broken up and re-formed several times, sometimes with different bassists and/or drummers. They disbanded for the first time after the release of their fifth album VI (1987), allowing Hetson to focus on Bad Religion (where he had been a member from 1984 to 2013) full-time. The Circle Jerks first reunited in 1994 and released their sixth and last studio album to date, Oddities, Abnormalities and Curiosities, the following year before separating for the second time. The band reunited for the second time in 2001 and spent the next ten years performing live periodically; this reunion lasted for only one new song, "I'm Gonna Live", which was released on their MySpace profile in 2007. Tensions among its members and failed attempts to record the follow-up to Oddities, Abnormalities and Curiosities resulted in the Circle Jerks breaking up yet again in 2011. However, the band announced in November 2019 that they will reunite in 2020 to celebrate the 40th anniversary of Group Sex with live shows.

events.title: Merry Mozart
events.description:
Journey to a place where personal expression and timeless beauty meet in radiant harmony as three composers reveal their most poetic and expressive selves.

Written as a birthday gift for his wife and first performed on Christmas morning, Richard Wagner’s Siegfried Idyll is a rare glimpse of the gentler side of the composer. Filled with tenderness and intimacy, the work is an idyllic unfolding of glowing harmonies, pastoral, calm, and deeply personal affection.

Ottorino Respighi’s Trittico Botticelliano brings three Renaissance paintings to vivid musical life. Inspired by Botticelli’s La Primavera, The Adoration of the Magi, and The Birth of Venus, Respighi’s orchestration shimmers with color and imagination, transforming visual beauty into sound that is refined, atmospheric, and richly evocative.

Mozart’s Symphony No. 39 is a work of noble warmth and exuberant invention. Majestic yet playful, the symphony balances ceremonial grandeur with lyric elegance, offering music that sparkles with clarity, wit, and humanity.

events.title: Circle Jerks x Repo Man
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
Circle Jerks x Repo Man

Sunday, December 6 | The Castro

Circle Jerks formed in Los Angeles in 1979 and quickly became one of the key bands of the early Southern California punk scene. Their debut album, Group Sex, came out in 1980 and remains one of the essential records of the era. More than 40 years later, Circle Jerks are still doing what they’ve always done—playing loud, fast and unapologetic punk rock.

That same Los Angeles punk scene is at the heart of Alex Cox’s 1984 film Repo Man. The movie follows Otto, a young punk who gets pulled into the bizarre world of car repossession while capturing a very specific version of early ’80s Los Angeles.

The night will start with a Circle Jerks set, followed by a Q&A with director Alex Cox, Keith Morris, and Zander Schloss (Kevin the Nerd and Circle Jerks bassist), then a screening of the cult classic Repo Man.

events.description: Jake Shimabukuro (born November 3, 1976, in Honolulu, Hawaii) is an American ukulele virtuoso and composer known for his fast and complex finger work. His music combines elements of jazz, blues, funk, rock, bluegrass, classical, folk, and flamenco. Shimabukuro has written numerous original compositions, including the entire soundtracks to two Japanese films, Hula Girls (2007) and the Japanese remake of Sideways (2009). Well known in Hawaii and Japan during his early solo career in the early 2000s, Shimabukuro became famous internationally in 2006, when a video of him playing a virtuosic rendition of "While My Guitar Gently Weeps" was posted on YouTube without his knowledge and became one of the first viral videos on that site. His concert engagements, collaborations with legendary musicians, media appearances, and music production have snowballed since then.

events.title: The Fretliners
events.description:
There is something happening between the mountains and the plains. A stirring in the dust. A song rising from the timber. Out of that landscape of grit and grace comes The Fretliners, a band carrying forward the oldest tradition in American music: telling the truth.

You can call them Colorado’s next great acoustic act. You can point to their Telluride and RockyGrass New Artist wins. You can talk about their musicianship, their harmonies, or their ability to command a room. All of those things are true. But they only tell part of the story.

The Fretliners are carving their own path through American music, drawing from bluegrass, Americana, folk, and rock to create something that feels both familiar and completely their own. Their songs carry the weight of long roads, changing seasons, lost loves, and the quiet hope that keeps people moving forward.

What separates The Fretliners is not just how they play, but what they have to say. Their writing feels rooted in something older than trends. They sing about places that shaped them, people who stayed, memories that linger, and the moments that remind us we are still connected to something real.

There is a kind of honesty in their music that cannot be manufactured. Each note feels lived-in,like old wood worn smooth by generations of hands. Each lyric feels like a conversation around a fire, a story passed down because it still matters.

The Fretliners are not chasing nostalgia. They are honoring what came before while creating...

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: Storefront Church
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

Storefront Church

Storefront Church is the project of Lukas Frank, who's drummed in Phoebe Bridgers' band and appeared on her albums, and the first song of his debut album As We Pass features DIIV frontman Cole Smith, but neither of those affiliations really prepares you for what to expect from As We Pass. It's a 9-song collection that's largely made up of bluesy, gothy, emo-y melancholic songs that sometimes sound like a cross between '90s Cure deep cuts and Nirvana Unplugged. (Lukas also cites Scott Walker as an influence, and you can hear that too.) Most of the album is bare-bones and somber, but Lukas also revs things up for the noise punk of "Faction from Under the Grove," and that fits right in too. With As We Pass, Lukas enters a long, line of depressive singer/songwriters, but even with over half a century of music like this, something about Lukas stands out. He grips you right off the bat with album opener "After the Alphabets" -- the kind of song that can make you drop everything and listen as soon as his voice comes in -- and the album stays that compelling throughout. Even with connections to established artists and the great Sargent House label behind him, this doesn't feel like the smash arrival of a hot new buzz artist; it's the subtle arrival of a songwriter whose songs creep up on you and knock you out when you're least expecting it. Usually, that's even better.

events.title: Spike Sikes and His Awesome Hotcakes: Holiday show
events.description:
Just The Right Recipe… The most frequently heard comment after a Spike’s Awesome Hotcakes gig goes something like this –
“No one is making this kind of music anymore!”
But what, exactly, is “this kind of music?”
Like hotcakes themselves, it goes by many names. Soul. Swing. Rhythm & Blues. Jazz. Jump. It’s a sound that’s classic and simple, but when it’s done right, it hits the spot, and has you grinning from ear to ear. Spike has spent years searching for this sound.
From the Texas blues joints he cut his teeth in to the funky halls of New Orleans, he was always studying the music, trying to find just the right recipe. It makes perfect sense that he found his bandmates in Sonoma County, a music scene that has fostered many eclectic artists for decades.
What he didn’t know was how hungry audiences were for “this kind of music.” You might say they’ve been eating it up like…Hotcakes!

events.title: Understanding Attachment Trauma & Building Resilience with Mindfulness
events.address: 5000 Sir Francis Drake Blvd Box 169,, Woodacre, CA, 94973
events.description:
with Pawan Bareja, PhD and Diane Poole Heller
We begin life with a child’s open heart, full of trust, innocence, and pure joy. Yet, over time, the world leaves its marks. We often arrive at our meditation cushions carrying a lifetime of hidden grief, from the lingering ache of a breakup to the quiet sorrow of a loveless childhood. To protect ourselves from this attachment trauma, we build walls that close us off from the very people we wish to love.
This daylong is an invitation to return home to the pure love that is your true nature. We do not heal in isolation; we heal together. Our nervous systems are beautifully social, wired to find safety, warmth, and co-regulation in the presence of others.
If accepting love feels foreign, you can break those protective patterns. Through guided meditations, gentle reflection, and supportive group connections, we will mend broken bonds, navigate love and conflict, and rebuild our lasting resilience.
Diane will lead a practical teaching session drawing on her background in nervous-system-informed approaches to attachment, offering an embodied complement to the day’s content.

The GLBT Historical Society Museum is pleased to partner with Unspeakable Vice to offer a monthly walking tour focused on the history of LGBTQIA+ resistance in the Castro neighborhood. Created by tour guide, former senior adjunct professor, and practicing designer Shawn Sprockett, Unspeakable Vice began as a close look at the queer origins of San Francisco, traversing the city’s North Beach and Barbary Coast areas to trace the history through from 1770-1960. This new tour closes a three-part story, extending Sprockett’s detailed and engaging storytelling to the Castro neighborhood.

Ten years after the White Night riots, the police came back. Meet the trans man doctors turned away, the lesbians who ran the blood drives and wards, and the community that answered a plague and two police riots with the same refusal. This tour includes a free round at the Lookout, overlooking the neighborhood you've just walked.

Details

Duration: about 90 minutes, plus the round afterward

Meet: GLBT Historical Society, 4127 18th Street

Ends: the Lookout, 3600 16th St at Market

Terrain: city sidewalks with one moderate hill; the Lookout is upstairs, stairs only

Ages: 21+ (free round, one per guest)

events.title: LIVE MUSIC: June McDoom
events.description:
Throwin’ Bo’s presents:

June McDoom

There is a hush most of us only knew as children, the warm drift between familiar household sounds and being carried to bed, a place that belongs to you and to some self you have not met yet. June McDoom's debut full-length, Follow the Light, lives in that dream space and then keeps walking, slipping out of time and waking somewhere new, barely familiar enough to feel like home yet wholly your own.

She came up in a Jamaican household on the edge of the Florida Everglades, an existence built of extended family, communal care, bass and harmonics. Her father, a carpenter and a student of sound, built his own speakers and kept three sound systems going across as many rooms. His low end would rise through her bedroom floor like some wayward cat while she lay above it with folk records, finding harmonies that were new and hers alone. Two musics in one room. Lushness as past and premonition.

She found folk on her own, somewhere between the cast recording of The Sound of Music and Simon and Garfunkel, while everyone around her called it sleepy music. She did not mind being the only one. The solitude let her fall for harmony first, before words, before anything else, and harmony is still the thing she reaches for.

Generationally speaking, the music was already in the air. Her grandfather, Colin Smith, is a distinguished mento man who played banjo and guitar and built his own rumba boxes, worked to keep Jamaica's oldest acoustic folk form alive....

events.title: Yaelokre
events.description:
Another Planet Entertainment presents
Yaelokre

Sunday, December 13 | The Castro

If you ever feel as if music has lost its capacity for surprise, the beguiling wonder and infinite creativity of Yaelokre will respark your belief. The Filipino-Icelandic artist – real name Keath Ósk (they/it) – fuses three imaginative strands to their visionary expression: intimate, innocent folk infused with leftfield surrealism and instant pop accessibility; artwork which is intricately detailed and beautifully alluring; and storytelling which brings personal experience and poetry into rich, fable-like narratives. What’s more, all three of these elements are crafted by this one visionary artist.

The scale of the fantastical world they have created is vast, both in terms of narrative and lore. But its essence is relatively simple. The songs are set in the fictional world of Meadowlark and chart the adventures of four masked children who comprise a musical ensemble known at The Lark: Cole Seymour, Clémente Dearworth, Peregrine August, and Kingsley. They perform as representatives of The Harkers, mythical beings who express the fundamental principles of nature, wonder and chaos. What’s more, Yaelokre voices all of the different characters within their universe.

Fork In The Path offers transformational foraging experiences in California for the adventurous of all ages.
Join us for a fun all-inclusive campout weekend filled with the fall foraged treasures of the Sierra Foothills, featuring acorns, bay nuts, plants, making natural sodas with wild yeasts and plants, weaving baskets from gourds and pine needles, and more!
Rosebud Ranch will be our home base for our weekend in Nevada City. They have a beautiful wooden bathhouse with hot showers, a cob wood-fired sauna, a fire pit with a stage for open mic (if you wish), and a shaded camping area. They are located just 5 minutes from the Hoyt Crossing of the glorious Yuba River, where you can swim in the limestone green waters to your heart’s content.
Three meals a day will be provided, which are a mix of foraged and farm-fresh ingredients.
Campout begins at 3pm on Thurs, and ends at 12 pm on Sunday, Oct 8-12th, 2026.

This is Your City. This is Your Voice. This is Your Future. Share your story about growing up and raising your family in San Francisco.

Every family has a story. Every voice matters. Please share yours.
Join us for the District 9 Mission Family Summit! The This Is Your City: Family Summit Series invites families, caregivers, young people, and community members from across San Francisco to help shape the future of our city.

Thursday, Oct. 8, 2026, 5:00 p.m. – 7:30 p.m.
The Women’s Building, 3543 18th Street, SF, CA 94110

District 9 Neighborhoods include: Mission District, Bernal Heights, the Portola, and the Calle 24 Latino Cultural District

events.title: SF Election 2026: Big Donors, Power Grabs + What Voters Need to Know
events.description:
League of Women Voters of San FranciscoWealthy special interests are trying to grab more power in San Francisco — whether they succeed is up to voters.
At a time when public oversight is shrinking and power is being concentrated fewer hands, understanding the role of large campaign donors in our political process has never been more urgent.
Join Joe Rivano Barros of Mission Local for an in-depth look at who is spending millions on San Francisco’s November 2026 ballot propositions in an effort to influence your vote. You’ll learn how these megadonors are trying to change the outcome of the election to serve the few, not the many.

After Joe’s presentation, Lila LaHood of the San Francisco Public Press will moderate a panel discussion on money in local politics with Darius Kemp of California Common Cause and Patrick Ford of the San Francisco Ethics Commission, with time for questions from the audience.
Speakers

Joe Rivano Barros, Executive Editor, Mission Local – Joe is an award-winning journalist whose coverage focuses on politics, campaign finance, Silicon Valley, and criminal justice. He received a B.A. at Stanford University for political science in 2014. He was born in Sweden, grew up in Chile, and moved to Oakland when he was eight.

events.title: Free KPFA Event: “The People’s History” Dave Zirin’s New Howard Zinn Biography (Oakland)
events.description:
Penguin Random HouseKPFA co-presents this evening celebrating the publication of The People’s Historian: The Outsized Life of Howard Zinn, by Dave Zirin, a columnist at The Nation.
​The new book examines the life and work of the iconic radical historian Howard Zinn, whose bestselling work, A People’s History of the United States, changed the way Americans saw the past.
​Despite its conservative critics, Zinn’s book changed the way that history is taught, as the New York Times admitted that it “left its mark for the better on many an American textbook written since.”

​Zirin will be joined at Local Economy by Davey D, journalist, hip hop historian, and host of Hard Knock Radio on KPFA.
​And of course, we’re co-hosting this one with East Bay Booksellers, who will be selling The People’s Historian.

events.title: The Black Cat Hotel: A Host of Vampires
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe Palace TheaterThe Black Cat Hotel has changed hands.
This Halloween, The Palace Theater‘s immersive Hotel returns under the care of new management – old money, impeccable manners, exclusively evening hours. Check in, receive the House Rules, and make your way room by room through live performances, hidden passages and increasingly questionable hospitality.

Returning guests may notice a few changes. The mirrors are being replaced. Garlic is temporarily unavailable. And the new staff only ever work nights.
Unlike a traditional stage show, The Black Cat Hotel unfolds around you. Performers may speak directly to you; rooms become scenes; and your small group moves through the story before eventually emerging into the Hotel bar. Most guests make it that far.
Come early for a drink. Stay afterwards if your nerves require another.
The staff are very much looking forward to having you.
October 8–31 · Show approx. 60 minutes / Allow 90 minutes for full experience · Tickets from $39 · Recommended for ages 16+

The Black Cat Hotel is an immersive theatrical experience, not an operating hotel. Overnight accommodation is not available, regardless of what the staff may tell you…

events.title: What’s At Stake: Free 2026 Ballot Breakdown (SF LGBT Center)
events.description:
rafikiThe 2026 election is closer than it feels, and the decisions on the ballot will shape health, housing, food access, and safety net programs for Black San Franciscans for years to come.
Join us for AACHEC’s Fall Civic Engagement Teach-In Series: a nonpartisan, community-centered conversation about what’s changing and what it means for you.
We’ll break down — in plain language — what’s on the ballot, what’s shifting in Medi-Cal, CalFresh, and federal housing programs, and what community members can do right now to make their voices heard.

events.title: Free “Syd Mead” Exhibition Opening: Sci-Fi Blade Runner Futurist (Transamerica Bldg.)
events.description:
Bright Future Arts, Syd Mead TrustFollowing its critically acclaimed 2025 debut in New York, Syd Mead: Future Pastime comes to the West Coast at the Transamerica Pyramid Annex Gallery, opening Thursday, October 8th, from 6pm to 8pm.
Few artists have shaped how the world pictures tomorrow as thoroughly as Syd Mead. For more than half a century, the self-described “visual futurist” set the vocabulary that designers, engineers, architects and filmmakers still draw on. He showed that the future could be drafted with precision rather than guessed at. That work began in industry, where Ford and U.S. Steel hired him to imagine what came next, and it reached millions through the films he helped design, among them Blade Runner, TRON and Aliens.
His gouache paintings show tomorrow with enough engineering logic to work as blueprints. But his real subject was never the machines. It was the people living with them: a casual drive through cerulean space, mechanical hounds racing above the skyscrapers, a dinner party in steel couture. Mead’s future is neither dystopian nor abstract. It is lived-in, leisurely and deeply human.

Thirty years after his last major Bay Area exhibition – just as the tools he forecast are finally arriving – Future Pastime asks San Francisco to reconsider the future it is building, and who it is for.
Syd Mead: Future Pastime runs 10/9 – 12/17, Weds-Sun, 11am-6pm.

events.title: Dying Fetus and Sanguisugabogg
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe UC TheatreDying Fetus
DYING FETUS established a reputation for uncompromising integrity with a slew of classic albums and today rides a resurgence of respect and esteem with a new generation. As Revolver Magazine wrote upon the release of their first new material since 2017’s Wrong One To Fuck With: “Their unique sound has always straddled the line between extreme metal instrumentation and heavy hardcore chugginess, and right now, they’re extremely well-regarded by many of today’s heavy-hitting hardcore acts, as well as their fair share of death metal and deathcore up-and-comers.”

Sanguisugabogg
Shat out of hell, indeed. That’s the sonic stench that permeates the epically unpronounceable, utterly indecipherable and altogether uncompromising sound of Ohio’s notorious gore-merchants, SANGUISUGABOGG. Homicidal Ecstasy, the ‘Bogg’s second Century Media platter of splatter isn’t merely a return to the “down-tuned drug death” that defined 2021’s Tortured Whole. It’s the fluid-streaked byproduct of a band that hit the road like crazed serial killers and never looked back as they plunged deeper into a celebration of Mortician-worshiping brutal death metal sounds and splatter classics like Dead-Alive. They also became a badass live and studio proposition in the process.

events.title: Odyssea
events.address: 9th and Lincoln Street, San Francisco, CA
events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerWe PlayersMeet CASEMA: The Conference Attending Society of Eleusinian Mystery Appreciators! A self-styled secret society, these massive fans of classical antiquity pose as hotel service workers in order to sneak into academic conferences and in this way be close to their erudite heroes and absorb some essence of their Olympic-level intellectual prowess. Our characters make the ancient myths their own through unique interpretations and stitch themselves into the lineage of homeric bards through telling their versions of the tales. Bringing themselves joy by taking it all very seriously and savoring silliness, these clowns know that like the Gods themselves we can be both sacred and ridiculous, solemn and irreverent, agnostic and devoted, petty and sincere, all at once. Perhaps this is the truth the Gods represent, that the Divine is all things, in all places, at all times, all at once.

events.description:
Aaron Coleman and Jon Cho-Polizzi discuss the challenges and revelations of translating the Black diaspora: examining continuities and ruptures across languages, geographies, and time. The global popularity of Black American culture can provide a reference point across the Black diaspora, but it also serves to obscure local traditions of art and resistance that have developed both independently and in conversation with other diasporic narratives over centuries.
Aaron will discuss his own work as a poet and its influence on his practice in the context of his 2024 translation of Afro-Cuban poet Nicolás Guillén’s The Great Zoo, while Jon reflects on the growing visibility of Black and Afro-German art and literature.

About Translator to Translator
Translator to Translator is a translator-curated event series at CAT featuring conversations about the intersections of literature, activism, and identity.
This event series places the Center for the Art of Translation’s (CAT’s) public programming resources directly into the hands of translators, empowering them to curate provocative and timely conversations about language, global literature, and the art of translation. By inviting guest curators to shape our programming, we are creating a space for dream interviews, deep investigations, and fresh perspectives on the work we love.

The 2026 lineup features regional projects by Dorothy Santos & Abram Stern, Ava Koohbor, Jean Carla Rodea, and EPOCH, alongside the touring projects of Sunken Cages and Rohan Chander.
SPAM 2026 is organized in collaboration with Indexical and SrcMaterial. Indexical is generously hosting the event, supporting the performances, and creating a space for gathering and relationality. SrcMaterial is curating Allaboration, a workshop series focused on technological literacy — with an emphasis on AI, collaboration, and connection in an era of increasingly asynchronous workspaces.
SPAM is an ongoing project of regrowth and persistence. We are committed to creating discourse from the margins, developing pathways of interconnectivity for our future selves.

events.title: Slow-Paced Golden Gate Park Ride w/ Adaptive Bikes
events.address: 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
BORP Adaptive Sports and RecreationSan Francisco shines in October! Let’s spend some time outside together and explore Golden Gate Park on wheels. San Francisco Village, BORP Adaptive Sports and Recreation, and the San Francisco Bicycle Coalition are partnering to bring together riders of all ages and will have bikes to available to meet your accessibility needs. This ride is perfect for elders, families with kids, and anyone who would like to enjoy the park on a beautiful Friday afternoon.
Let us know what would help you join us – BORP will provide recumbent electric assist bikes, tandem side by side bikes, bikes with recumbent seats, and more! If you have a body, we’ll do our best to find a bike with the right fit/support. If you are borrowing an accessible bike, plan to get to the Bandshell by 2:00 PM to sign a waiver and find the right fit. If you want to partner with someone to help them ride, let us know and come by 2:00 PM.
You are also welcome to bring and ride your own bike! The pace will be slow and conversational and we don’t drop anyone. The route can be found at https://ridewithgps.com/routes/56763052. Organizers request you wear a helmet as well; BORP will have some available for those using an accessible bike.

events.title: Remains a Memory
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerLara AburamadanRemains a Memory is a still photo collection from Gaza City, encapsulating a placethat holds stories of the land and the sea. Within the frames, serene moments unfold against a backdrop that longs for genuine peace—a rarity in the artist’s hometown.
In this show, Lara Aburamadan explores the transformation of memories of home shaped by the relentless impact of war, transitioning from tangible reality to the ethereal realms of daydreams and nostalgia. Having lived in exile for years, Aburamadan is left pondering the uncertain path ahead, questioning the fate of a Gaza that clings to memories of people and places that don’t exist anymore.

REMAINS A MEMORY FILM

events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
events.description:
Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
Yerba Buena Partnership
San Francisco has officially turned a downtown building into a giant art projector.

Yerba Buena Illuminated launched Tuesday, August 25, 2026 projecting giant digital artworks onto the historic Humboldt Bank Building at 785 Market St., at the top of Yerba Buena Lane. The massive projection covers a 95-foot-high by 46-foot-wide section of the building, turning one of Market Street’s historic facades into a giant outdoor art screen.

The free outdoor art show runs nightly from twilight until 10 p.m., with the first artwork on view for about 90 days. The inaugural projection is Jennifer Steinkamp’s It’s a nice day for a white wedding. (2008), from SFMOMA’s collection. Inspired by Billy Idol’s “White Wedding,” the digital artwork covers the Beaux-Arts-style building with a cascade of animated red, white and yellow wedding flowers.

The project is a collaboration between Yerba Buena Partnership, SFMOMA, the Museum of the African Diaspora and Yerba Buena Center for the Arts. And this first installation is just the beginning: MoAD and YBCA will curate future projections in 2027, so the giant building-as-canvas is sticking around.
The projection is designed to serve as a giant welcome sign for the Yerba Buena arts district, home to more than 60 public artworks and some of San Francisco’s biggest cultural institutions. The rotating projections will continue to light up the Humboldt Bank Buildi...

events.title: Step Into Wonder – Deep Dive Workshop
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerPriscila Soares

Go beyond the surface of creativity with Step Into Wonder: Deep Dive, an intimate, guided art experience for adults at Mare Island Art Studios.
Led by artist Priscila Soares, this three-hour session uses art-making, creative prompts and reflection to explore what happens when we quiet the inner critic, let go of expectations and give ourselves permission to create freely.

No artistic experience is needed. The focus isn’t on making something “good”—it’s on curiosity, expression and discovering what can emerge when you stop trying to control the outcome.
Set within the immersive Step Into Wonder installation, surrounded by glowing sculptures and a transformed gallery environment, the Deep Dive offers a smaller, more intentional experience for those who want to explore the deeper side of The Letting Go Art Experience.
Come as you are. Get messy. Follow your intuition. See what happens when you let go.
October 10 & 24 • 10 AM–1 PM18+ • $45 • Limited to 15 participantsMare Island Art Studios, 110 Pintado St., Vallejo

events.title: Free Outdoor Painting Gathering at the Palace of Fine Arts
events.description:
© Out There WatercolorsFree outdoor painting gathering at the Palace of Fine Arts.
Come paint with us. Sign up at Painters Unite to hear about future gatherings.
Painters Unite is a free gathering for anyone who wants to slow down and paint outdoors, together. No class, no pressure, nothing for sale.
I’m Marco Flavio, a watercolor teacher here in the city. I started this because so many people told me they wanted more time to paint and to be around others, and I think that shouldn’t have to cost anything. I’ll be painting right alongside you, same as everyone.

This time we’re meeting at the Palace of Fine Arts, at the intersection of Baker Street and Beach Street at 10AM. From there we’ll have a beautiful view across the lagoon toward the Palace, with the architecture, water, and reflections all in front of us. It’s a great opportunity to play with reflections in watercolor and simplify a pretty spectacular scene into a painting.
As always, I’ll bring a few small challenges, different ways of seeing and painting what’s in front of us. I’ll also have a limited number of pre-drawings of the Palace of Fine Arts on watercolor paper, first come, first served, for beginners who’d like a starting point. Take a challenge, use a pre-draw, or simply find a spot and paint. No experience needed.

events.title: Bridging The Gap: An Evening of Indian Music
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerNazan Aktaswith Nazan Aktas (Cello) & William Rossel (Tabla)
​Nazan Aktas (cello) & William Rossel (tabla) will present a performance of afternoon and evening ragas in the styles of the North Indian, Maihar and Lucknow gharanas. This performance will highlight the versatility of the cello and tabla as both solo and accompanying instruments, as each player will take turns accompanying the other. The cello (being a relatively new instrument to Indian music) and tabla together will bridge the gap between old & new in the hopes of sharing the beautiful music of the North Indian Classical tradition.
​In Person Only at the SF Dharma Collective, 2929 24th Street.

​Nazan Aktas is a cellist based in Northern California who has performed with many artists, ensembles and orchestras throughout the Bay Area and beyond. She has been studying at the Ali Akbar College of Music since 2015, under the tutelage of Alam Khan, son of Maestro Ali Akbar Khan. She has also studied vocal music with Ranjana Ghatak, disciple of Pandit Ajoy Chakraborty and received further instruction from cellist Saskia Rao-de Haas, who studied with Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia. She is a graduate of Sonoma State University, with a Bachelor of Music Degree with a double concentration in Performance and Jazz Studies and has a Master’s Degree from Berklee College of Music in Contemporary Performance.

events.title: Litquake: Claudia Rankine: Triage
events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizer

The award-winning author of Citizen: An American Lyric returns with a new genre-defying work blending essay, memoir, and visual art

Sponsored by Alta Journal

Poet Claudia Rankine’s work is unfailingly expansive—broadening readers’ understanding of race, social conscience, and the limits of genre. Triage, Rankine’s first book since the groundbreaking “American” trilogy (whose centerpiece, Citizen, was a 2023 Alta California Book Club selection), is another boundary-defying work. Here Rankine traces a decades-long friendship between two women—the narrator and the theorist—following their evolving relationship against the background of ever-more-turbulent times.
In an uncategorizable mix of essay, criticism, memoir, and photography, Rankine creates a politically urgent book that Booklist calls “Startlingly original … A remarkable, soul-stirring work.” Joining Rankine in conversation is Cathy Park Hong, whose award-winning nonfiction book Minor Feelings engages intimately with Rankine’s ideas. The Alta Journal team will be on hand to introduce you to upcoming California Book Club selections, and we’ll kick things off with performances by 2026 Oakland Youth Poet Laureate Isaiah Kahn and Vice OYPL Isabel Shen. Doors at 6:30pm.

events.title: Climate Wayfinding: Healing Ourselves and the Planet We Call Home
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerKatharine WilkinsonAre You Climate Concerned and Looking for a Place to Land?
If you’re carrying climate grief, uncertainty, or even an awareness of possible collapse, you don’t have to carry it alone. East Bay friends are warmly invited to join me for a guided exploration of Dr. Katharine K. Wilkinson’s Climate Wayfinding: Healing Ourselves and the Planet We Call Home.
This is more than a traditional book club. Through essays, poetry, art, music, facilitated conversation, and reflection, we’ll explore how to move from climate ache and overwhelm toward courage, connection, possibility, and meaningful action.

I’m Heidi Harmon; a longtime climate organizer and former three-term mayor who recently moved to Oakland to deepen my community-based work. After 25 years in the climate movement, I believe the relationships we build are as essential to our resilience as any policy we pass.
Sundays, beginning October 11
10:00 a.m.–12:00 p.m.
In person in Oakland. 2310 Telegraph Ave, Oakland, CA 94612
Donation-based; no one turned away for lack of funds
Thanks to the generosity of author Dr. Wilkinson, also co-editor of All We Can Save, the first eight people to register will receive a complimentary copy of the book.
If there is enough interest, I would also be happy to create a separate virtual group. Message me with questions or to express interest in joining online.
Come find your footing and your people for the road ahead.

events.title: “Welcome Back Monarch” Butterfly Festival 2026 (Santa Cruz)
events.address: 2531 W Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
events.description:
Santa Cruz State BeachesWelcome Back Monarch Festival is a free family event at Natural Bridges State Beach featuring crafts, hands-on learning, a parade, story time, games, live music, food trucks, hand-cranked pumpkin ice cream, and items for sale. The 2026 festival also includes a screening of “Creating the West Marin Monarch Sanctuary,” a monarch photo exhibit by Elizabeth Weber, and a talk by Julia Butterfly Hill. Free cake is listed on the event flyer; parking costs $10.
The Monarchs return every year around mid October and typically stay for 3-4 months.
Every fall and winter, Natural Bridges State Beach welcomes back the monarchs to their winter habitat in the eucalyptus grove, the only State Monarch Preserve in California. Starting in early to mid-October, the black and orange beauties start trickling in from colder climates to enjoy our moderate coastal weather. Scientifically speaking, monarchs are tropical butterflies and at no point in their life cycle – egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly – can they freeze, so they move with the warmer weather while migrating south.

Natural Bridges State Beach is California’s only state park designated as a monarch preserve, featuring a protected canyon eucalyptus grove and an accessible 0.4-mile trail.

events.title: SF’s Annual Italian Heritage Festival & Parade 2026
events.address: Jefferson and Taylor, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
Italian Heritage Festival & ParadeThe San Francisco Italian Heritage Parade returns to the streets of San Francisco on Sunday, October 11, 2026, bringing Italian-American culture, music, performances, floats, and community groups to the streets of North Beach.
The San Francisco Italian Heritage Parade is the longest continuously running Italian Heritage Parade in the United States and celebrates the accomplishments and culture of Italian-Americans. The inaugural parade took place in 1868 in downtown San Francisco, featuring bands and marching units from Italian fraternal organizations. Throughout the years, the parade has remained a celebration of the vitality of Italian communities throughout the Bay Area.
Parade Route
The parade begins at 12:30 p.m. at the foot of Jefferson and Powell Streets in Fisherman’s Wharf, then proceeds through North Beach along Columbus Avenue before ending in Washington Square in front of Saints Peter and Paul Church. Parade viewing is available throughout the entire route.

The celebration features Italian and Italian-American dignitaries, live Italian music, performances, floats, and representatives from Italian and Italian-American organizations and businesses. Admission is free.

events.address: W. MacArthur Blvd. and Webster St., Oakland, CA
events.description:
Sarah Bush Dance ProjectAs the pilot performance of The Dyke HERstory Dance Tour, PITCH a new, site-specific dance theater project exploring Bay Area queer history through movement, storytelling, and community engagement. Set on the softball field, five dancers embody Bay Area dyke ancestors reuniting as an all-star “ghost team.” Each player steps up to bat, sharing her story through recorded audio and embodied movement as the ensemble rounds the bases in a collective portrait of queer community, remembrance, and play. Directed and choreographed by Sarah Bush with research lead by KJ Dahlaw, the work features an original live score by KKINGBOO and B. Dukes of 7000COILS, the Oakland-based, Black-owned, gender-expansive collective.
Created by the multiracial, intergenerational, and queer-led artists of Sarah Bush Dance Project,
PITCH celebrates the enduring legacy of Bay Area lesbian softball as both a cultural touchstone and a place of belonging. The work emerges at a critical moment, as many queer elders who helped build lesbian and dyke communities in Oakland and San Francisco are aging while their stories remain largely absent from public archives and artistic representation. Rather than treating history as something fixed, PITCH invites audiences to experience remembrance as a living, joyful, and embodied act.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerAndrea Prichett & FriendsIn an evening with Andrea Prichett and Friends, you can expect to be taken on something of a journey. From tender ballads to raucous political anthems, the performance moves between the personal and the political and sometimes both at the same time.
The rich resonance of Andrea’s voice carries the message of her original lyrics on a versatile instrumental foundation provided by Deborah Hungerford on piano and keyboards, Mike Derrick on guitar, and Alexis Tsamoudakis on bass. The genre defying tunes range from blues, folk, rock and even jazz at times. While Andrea’s influences include singer-songwriters (Patti Griffin, Tracy Chapman, Joni Mitchell, James Taylor, etc), she also loves to dance and so the R&B/Motown sound is also woven into the mix.

Formerly of the Berkeley-based, nationally-known feminist folk trio Rebecca Riots, Andrea has released several albums. In recent times, Andrea released a solo album, The Frame, and continues to write and sing about the issues of the day. A natural storyteller and political activist, Andrea combines anecdotes with her carefully crafted songs to inspire and uplift her audiences. Her fans describe the experience of going to her shows as part political, part spiritual, part humorous and TOTALLY engaging!

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerProfs and PintsProfs and Pints San Francisco presents: “The Rise of Vampires,” on the folkloric origins and literary evolution of today’s fanged fiends, with Sara Hackenberg, professor of English at San Francisco State University and scholar of Victorian literature and literature’s vampire tradition.
Did you know that vampires sprang from literature nearly a whole century before Bram Stoker wrote Dracula, and that they prowled in folklore for centuries before that?

You’d have to visit a lot of gravesites to witness the unearthing of as many vampires as will be raised at the October 12th debut of Profs and Pints at The Dairy community space at San Francisco’s Presidio Sports Basement.
The excavation will be carried out by Professor Sara Hackenberg, who previously has given excellent Profs and Pints talks on vampires and Christmas ghost stories.
She’ll show you the vampire beneath the vampire beneath the vampire, tracing their evolution in old European folklore and the English literature of the nineteenth-century.
You’ll get to know the seductive, snaky Lamia in Samuel Taylor Coleridge’s 1816 poem “Christabel” and the sapphic seductress at the center of Joseph Sheridan Le Fanu’s 1872 novella Carmilla. You’ll spend time with the mad, bad, and dangerous Byronic vampire that originated in John Polidori’s 1819 gothic horror story “The Vampyre,” found his way into theatrical adaptations such as James Planché’s 1820 “The Bride of the Isles,” and then...

About Bota Tapas and Paella Bar

As an age-old tradition dating back to the early 1800s, Spanish travelers used “BOTA”, or traditional sheep-skinned repositories, to transport and share their wine. The Spaniards historically thrived on the values of sharing and community: two ideals that have buoyantly withstood the test of time. Tailored around these same ideals are Spain’s cuisine and the development of “tapas,” style dining – where individuals share small plates and memories. From Seville to San Francisco, and across the world, our goal is to initiate more memories – this is why and how we operate. Whether it be with your friends or family, we here at Bota sincerely hope that you enjoy this stop on your journey.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerNortheastern UniversityDr. Paula Goldman is the Chief Ethical & Humane Use Officer at Salesforce and a trained anthropologist. Over the last several years, she focused her research on how AI is being implemented in companies of all sizes and all around the world.
The result is her new book, Manage the Machine: How to Harness Human-AI Collaboration at Work. From a local council in the UK to a bank in Singapore, Dr. Goldman explores successes and failures. It all leads to her central case: human judgment is more important than ever, and organizations need to keep their people at the center of their strategies.

events.title: SF’s “Circus By The Bay” Night: History Panel + Wild Live Acts (Fort Mason)
events.description:
Fort Mason Center for Arts & CultureCowell Theater hosts a panel conversation and live performances exploring San Francisco’s new American circus movement. Pickle Family Circus and New Pickle Circus veterans Gypsy Snider, Shana Carroll, Jeff Raz, and Tandy Beal will discuss the scene’s history, alongside archival photos and video and performances by artists from Prescott Circus, Dear San Francisco, Circus Bella, and San Francisco Youth Circus.
Original Event Description:
CIRCUS BY THE BAY
Panel conversation and live performances
Tuesday, October 13, 2026 – 7:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m.
Cowell Theater, Pier 2/Gateway Pavilion, FMCAC, RESERVE SPACE
In the 1970s, San Francisco became an epicenter of the emerging new American circus – an intimate one-ring model that spurned animal acts and focused on traditional skills of juggling, clowning, acrobatics, and aerial work, all filtered through a countercultural vaudevillian sensibility. This “not-so-big-top” was pioneered by such local companies as the Pickle Family Circus and its later incarnation, the New Pickle Circus, which performed annually at Fort Mason Center For Arts & Culture, and longtime FMCAC residents Make*A*Circus. This movement spawned a stream of Bay Area talents that spread their influence from Cirque du Soleil and Broadway to movies, and TV, an impact which resonates to this day.

Please join us for the next session of The Science Scoop, a quarterly public lecture series hosted by UCSF Basic Sciences. Discovery for ALL!
We invite you to learn about how curiosity-driven research is leading to critical medical advances. Through engaging lectures geared towards a lay audience, premier researchers at the University of California, San Francisco will share the challenges and joys of making scientific discoveries and their impact on bettering human health. The audience will have the opportunity to ask questions at the end of the talk.
This is a FREE lecture open to the general public, and all are welcome. No tickets or registration needed.

The Speaker
Holly A. Ingraham, PhD, is the Herzstein Professor of Molecular Physiology at the University of California, San Francisco. Her research focuses on hormone-responsive nodes in the brain and peripheral tissues that impact metabolic, skeletal, and gut physiology and women’s health. Through question-driven basic science, Ingraham has uncovered how hormonal fluctuations lead to adaptive responses in females across their lifespan. Ingraham is an elected fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science and a member of the National Academy of Sciences and the American Academy of Arts and Sciences. She earned her Ph.D. from UCSD.
https://ingrahamlab.ucsf.edu/

events.title: Reimagining Local News: From the Ground Up with Tiny News Collective
events.address: 988 Market St, 9th Floor, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
kalw

Join Tiny News Collective for a conversation with the community-centered founders rebuilding and reimagining local news.

From the Ground Up: The Founders Reimagining Local News
You already know one story about local news: outlets shrinking and closing, and chains buying up what remains.
But across the country, and here in San Francisco, a different story is being written. Founders are building small, independent newsrooms in the places they live, accountable to their neighbors. A form of community infrastructure, built on trust: tiny news.

Join us for a panel with Tiny News Collective executive director Amy Kovac-Ashley, COYOTE Media Collective co-founder Soleil Ho, News Relay Network co-founder Daphne Magnawa, and News Futures lead steward Darryl Holliday. They’ll discuss new research on what it takes for tiny newsrooms to launch and last, and why these types of newsrooms are critical for the future of journalism and democracy.
KALW @ Warfield Commons
998 Market St., San Francisco
Doors open at 6:00
Program begins at 6:30
Refreshments will be served
The event is free with an RSVP — and you are welcome to make a donation meaningful to you.

Submitted by the Event OrganizerCredit Smoke Door Lake TahoeWhat happens when two chefs from very different culinary traditions meet around a shared fascination with cooking over fire?
For one night only, Chef Earth (Saritwat Wanvichitkun) and Pastry Chef Pond (Chayanin Tanapradit) of Bangkok’s Saawaan are coming to Lake Tahoe for a special collaboration with Chef Koji Hanada and Pastry Chef/Culinary Director Matt Tinder of Smoke Door Lake Tahoe.

Saawaan is one of Bangkok’s acclaimed contemporary Thai restaurants, having held a Michelin star for four consecutive years. Its tasting menu explores regional Thai flavors through techniques including fermenting, steaming, boiling and charcoal grilling. Chef Earth, a Phuket native trained in both French and Thai cooking, leads the savory kitchen, while Chef Pond brings a pastry approach that combines classical technique with Thai ingredients and flavors.
Recently, Earth has become increasingly interested in wood-fire cooking and the possibilities it opens up, making Smoke Door – and its fire-driven kitchen in the mountains – a particularly interesting place for this collaboration.
Rather than creating a conventional fusion menu, the chefs will cook side by side across eight courses, alternating between Saawaan and Smoke Door. The dinner becomes a conversation between two distinct perspectives: Earth’s modern interpretation of Thai cuisine and Koji’s contemporary Japanese cooking, connected by a shared curiosity about fire.

Hierse’s writing navigates the complexities of life in contemporary Germany, exploring links between language, place, and belonging across generations. Her works are characterized by complex ambiguities, settings and narratives that compound and merge, demonstrating unexpected connections and continuities. Together they will discuss Hierse‘s explorations of German and Chinese entanglements in her writing, the role of Chinatowns across the diaspora, and the publication of her works in English translation in new and forthcoming anthologies.
Lin Hierse

Lin Hierse is a prolific author, journalist, poet, and public intellectual. With a background in Asian Studies and Human Geography, she is a longtime contributor to several major German journals and periodicals; she wrote the biweekly column “Poetical Correctness” in taz from 2020-2023. Her acclaimed autofictional debut novel Wovon wir träumen [What We Dream Of] was published in 2022 and follows the interconnected stories of three generations of women whose lives are ruptured and reunited through the experience of migration and life in the Chinese diaspora. events.description:
Submitted by the Event Organizeralliance Française de San FranciscoAt the dawn of the twentieth century, the antisemitism of totalitarian regimes compelled many Jewish composers from Central and Eastern Europe into exile. Fleeing pogroms and persecution, they settled in the United States—the new Promised Land—and found their way to Hollywood. Musicians such as Max Steiner, Erich Wolfgang Korngold, Franz Waxman, Miklós Rózsa, Bronisław Kaper, Irving Berlin, and Dimitri Tiomkin established their distinctive musical voice there. Trained in the European classical tradition, they fused it with American culture and the idioms of jazz. Bridging the legacy of the “world of yesterday” and the spirit of modernity, they helped shape the art of film scoring and left an enduring imprint on Hollywood’s Golden Age (1930s–1960s).

events.title: LitquakeE: A 22nd-Century Conservation Ethos for California
events.description:
kalwTogether, let’s imagine a new conservation ethos—one rooted in restoration, resilience, and reciprocity
Sponsored by Heyday Books
Co-presented with LITQUAKE

California’s landscapes have long been shaped by deep relationships between people and place. But that relationship has changed dramatically over time, especially with the rise of European American settlement and the erasure of Traditional Ecological Knowledge. Panelists Obi Kaufmann, creator of the California Field Atlas series; Laura Cunningham, award-winning author of A State of Change; and earth scientist and professional mountain biker Dillon Osleger examine how modern society has grown increasingly estranged from the natural world. Together, they imagine a new conservation ethos—one rooted in restoration, resilience, and reciprocity—and ask what it would take for Californians to leave the state healthier, more biodiverse, and more ecologically whole at the end of the 21st century than at its beginning. Moderated by Leslie Carol Roberts. Doors at 6:30pm.

Italian-born, New York-based jazz singer and composer Chiara Izzi has developed a distinctive musical identity shaped by her Italian roots, deep connection to Brazilian music, and ability to sing and speak in Italian, Portuguese, and English. Her breakthrough came when she won first prize at the prestigious Montreux Jazz Festival Vocal Competition, a victory personally awarded by legendary musician Quincy Jones, who chaired the jury. The following year, Chiara returned to the festival to perform and open for the iconic Paco de Lucía. The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.

events.title: Glaive – God Save the Three Tour
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe UC TheatreFrom his beginnings in Hendersonville, North Carolina (population 15k), to opening for The Kid LAROI on The First Time tour last year, glaive has become a name synonymous with a scene that redefines pop, not by distancing itself from tradition but by forging a new, innovative style. His previous works, including cypress grove, all dogs go to heaven, and then i’ll be happy, have all cemented him as a standout artist, lauded by the likes of The New York Times, Vulture, GQ and The FADER.

His 2nd studio album released in late 2024, May It Never Falter, was hailed as a genre-defying body of work that marked the beginning of an independent chapter in his artistry. Working closely with a tight-knit team of collaborators including John Cunningham (XXXTENTACION, Kanye West), Ralph Castelli (Dora Jar, The Neighbourhood), and Jeff Hazin (Kali Uchis, renforshort) the album served as a coming-of-age narrative set against the backdrop of adolescence and self-discovery. May It Never Falter was recorded in the remote landscapes of Iceland and Wales, continuing the Sigur Rós-inspired approach to isolated, immersive recording environments that began with his debut album i care so much i don’t care at all (2023). The album was listed as one of the best of 2024 by Vogue Magazine and was supported by a North American and European tour in spring of 2025.

events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
events.description:
Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
Yerba Buena Partnership
San Francisco has officially turned a downtown building into a giant art projector.

Yerba Buena Illuminated launched Tuesday, August 25, 2026 projecting giant digital artworks onto the historic Humboldt Bank Building at 785 Market St., at the top of Yerba Buena Lane. The massive projection covers a 95-foot-high by 46-foot-wide section of the building, turning one of Market Street’s historic facades into a giant outdoor art screen.

The free outdoor art show runs nightly from twilight until 10 p.m., with the first artwork on view for about 90 days. The inaugural projection is Jennifer Steinkamp’s It’s a nice day for a white wedding. (2008), from SFMOMA’s collection. Inspired by Billy Idol’s “White Wedding,” the digital artwork covers the Beaux-Arts-style building with a cascade of animated red, white and yellow wedding flowers.

The project is a collaboration between Yerba Buena Partnership, SFMOMA, the Museum of the African Diaspora and Yerba Buena Center for the Arts. And this first installation is just the beginning: MoAD and YBCA will curate future projections in 2027, so the giant building-as-canvas is sticking around.
The projection is designed to serve as a giant welcome sign for the Yerba Buena arts district, home to more than 60 public artworks and some of San Francisco’s biggest cultural institutions. The rotating projections will continue to light up the Humboldt Bank Buildi...

events.venue: First United Methodist Church of Palo Alto
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSan Francisco Chamber OrchestraProgram:
Ludwig van Beethoven – Coriolan Overture, Op. 62
Grace Williams – Sea Sketches
Ludwig van Beethoven – Symphony No. 3 in Eb Major, Op. 55 “Eroica”

Betrayed by Napoleon’s thirst for power, Beethoven furiously tore apart his 3rd Symphony’s dedication, and in doing so created a work that captured, like no other, the defiant and life-affirming heroic spirit. With its massive size and emotional power, the Eroica Symphony would change the course of Classical music forever.
Our program begins with the Coriolan Overture, Beethoven’s electrifying portrait of Shakespeare’s doomed warrior followed by Grace William’s hauntingly beautiful Sea Sketches, which paint the Welsh coastline in all its wild, shimmering glory.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerjwBECAUSE I HAVE TO is a discussion series featuring Bay Area artists, writers, musicians, chefs, and creators who work across multiple artistic and creative mediums, against the grain of their professional lives, alongside it, or within it. Hosted by Jeff Wright, these conversations will delve into creative work in the modern age, the real whys that drive us to make it, how it intertwines with our lives, and what really makes it all possible.

BIHT #1 will feature Amar Lal and Paolo Bicchieri. If you’re in the Bay Area, their fingerprints are probably already on something familiar to you, due to their presence and commitment to culture and creative work here. Professionally, Amar is fine-tuning and refining songs we listen to at his Oakland studio every day. He also creates visual works of art to express sound, as noted in his latest book, Practicing Joy. Paolo’s creative writing can be found in any given news outlet, narrating underrepresented projects, or throughout his handful of published poetry works. He also organizes community events to uplift local poets, writers, and up-and-coming chefs through Kitchen Table. All of this work takes perseverance, the right settings, creative discipline, and much more that we are set to discuss in the first edition of BECAUSE I HAVE TO.

Every bird holds a memory. Every memory holds a meaning. Across different cultures and communities, across time and space, birds have played a significant role in shaping our understanding of the world, ourselves, and our relationship in nature.
On Sunday, October 18th, this year’s Berkeley Bird Festival invites you to celebrate our incredible birdlife here in the Bay Area through the theme of “Myth and Memories”.
Get outside and witness the birds and our shared environment. Engage with the Myth of the Flying Africans. Fold a crane for peace and longevity. Hear the story of SF’s Wild Parrots. Watch the street “split the sky” through a dance inspired by migration. Listen to the science behind wildlife and remember, every feather, past and present, is a portal to a world where all of us thrive.
This festival brings science, art, and culture under its wing to inspire our collective imagination and action in protecting birds and our environment. We hope you’ll join us whether you’re bird-curious or a long-time advocate.
Register in advance to attend a trip, or gather your flock, swoop in, and dive into a world of birds, Myth and Memory.

events.venue: San Francisco Public Library Main Library, 4th floor
events.description:
Inventurous
Transform everyday film plastics into durable, leather-like sheets using heat and pressure. Learn how to fuse materials such as newspaper delivery bags and soft plastic packaging into reusable textiles that can be cut, sewn, and shaped like fabric. Tara de la Garza of Inventurous demonstrates the process and shares creative ways to repurpose plastic waste into functional projects.
Inventurous is a community-based organization that transforms locally sourced plastic waste into useful, high-value products. By engaging community members in collecting, sorting, and processing discarded plastics, Inventurous demonstrates practical approaches to reducing waste through creative reuse.

events.title: MainStage 1: Beethoven’s Eroica, A Hero’s Journey
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSan Francisco Chamber OrchestraProgram:
Ludwig van Beethoven – Coriolan Overture, Op. 62
Grace Williams – Sea Sketches
Ludwig van Beethoven – Symphony No. 3 in Eb Major, Op. 55 “Eroica”

Betrayed by Napoleon’s thirst for power, Beethoven furiously tore apart his 3rd Symphony’s dedication, and in doing so created a work that captured, like no other, the defiant and life-affirming heroic spirit. With its massive size and emotional power, the Eroica Symphony would change the course of Classical music forever.
Our program begins with the Coriolan Overture, Beethoven’s electrifying portrait of Shakespeare’s doomed warrior followed by Grace William’s hauntingly beautiful Sea Sketches, which paint the Welsh coastline in all its wild, shimmering glory.

events.address: 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.title: Rocky Horror Picture Show with a Full Shadow Cast (SF Main Library)
events.description:
Rocky Horror Picture Show
The Bawdy Caste performs a full shadow cast of The Rocky Horror Picture Show, acting out the movie in front of the screen while it plays with audience participation. Expect singing, dancing, costumes, callbacks and a room full of people ready to celebrate. Callbacks are the shouted responses that Rocky Horror audiences have traded with the screen for 50 years. Don’t worry if you don’t know them yet — the crowd will teach you. Dressing up is encouraged.
Official participation kits, Bawdy Bags, available for purchase for $5. These include everything you need to throw, blow, and glow during the show. You may bring props, but no wet items, meat, rice, toast, glitter, confetti, or anything that could make a mess or attract critters.
Doors at 5 p.m.; film starts at 5:45 p.m.

Bawdy Caste, a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit, has been San Francisco’s Rocky Horror Shadowcast for three decades. Their performances are based in SF and can be found across the Bay and beyond.

events.title: Bat Week Screening of ‘The Invisible Mammal’
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe Invisible Mammal

Award-winning documentary highlights global bat extinction crisis

The Citizens Environmental Council invites you to a free screening of an award-winning documentary highlighting the fight to save North American bats on Wednesday, October 21, from 6 to 8 p.m. at the Burlingame Community Center at 850 Burlingame Ave. in Burlingame. There is no charge for admission, but pre-registration is required. Watch the trailer below!

Just in time for Halloween – and Bat Week! – “The Invisible Mammal” focuses on the plight of several species of North American bats now at risk because of a deadly fungal disease called White-nose Syndrome (WNS) and a team of women biologists determined to rescue these rapidly vanishing species. After a screening of the 90-minute film, filmmaker Kristin Tièche will offer insights and answer questions about a strategy called Operation Fat Bat, pioneered by women scientists, that could rebuild healthy bat populations across North America.
Bats save U.S. agriculture billions of dollars in pesticide use each year, and the decline of bat populations is linked to an increase in infant mortality where these pesticides are used. Since 2006, WNS has decimated bat populations across 42 states and Canada, killing millions of bats.

events.title: Free Panel: Bay Area Protest Photojournalists + Pop-Up Exhibit (SF Main Library)
events.description:
Steve DisenhofPhotojournalists on the Front Lines of Protest: A panel discussion hosted by Indivisible San Francisco and Pro Bono Photo.
Indivisible SF presents a panel of local photojournalists from Pro Bono Photo and other news organizations who will share selections from their portfolios and discuss the role photojournalism plays in documenting protest, civic action and pro-democracy movements.
From the civil rights and voting rights movements of the 1960s to today’s social justice actions, the San Francisco Bay Area has long been a significant site of protest and civil disobedience. Who documents these fleeting moments of protest and civic action? Local photojournalists share their experiences covering pro-democracy movements and street demonstrations throughout the Bay Area.

Hear firsthand accounts from photographers documenting recent protests and demonstrations, view a curated projection of their work and engage directly with the panelists during an audience Q&A.
Pop-Up Gallery: A selection of photographs by participating photojournalists will be displayed alongside historical protest photography from SFPL collections, connecting contemporary documentation of Bay Area demonstrations with the Library’s photographic record of protest and civic action. The display will be on view on the 4th Floor of the Main Library from Sept. 17–Dec. 31.

Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
events.description:
Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
Yerba Buena Partnership
San Francisco has officially turned a downtown building into a giant art projector.

Yerba Buena Illuminated launched Tuesday, August 25, 2026 projecting giant digital artworks onto the historic Humboldt Bank Building at 785 Market St., at the top of Yerba Buena Lane. The massive projection covers a 95-foot-high by 46-foot-wide section of the building, turning one of Market Street’s historic facades into a giant outdoor art screen.

The free outdoor art show runs nightly from twilight until 10 p.m., with the first artwork on view for about 90 days. The inaugural projection is Jennifer Steinkamp’s It’s a nice day for a white wedding. (2008), from SFMOMA’s collection. Inspired by Billy Idol’s “White Wedding,” the digital artwork covers the Beaux-Arts-style building with a cascade of animated red, white and yellow wedding flowers.

The project is a collaboration between Yerba Buena Partnership, SFMOMA, the Museum of the African Diaspora and Yerba Buena Center for the Arts. And this first installation is just the beginning: MoAD and YBCA will curate future projections in 2027, so the giant building-as-canvas is sticking around.
The projection is designed to serve as a giant welcome sign for the Yerba Buena arts district, home to more than 60 public artworks and some of San Francisco’s biggest cultural institutions. The rotating projections will continue to light up the Humboldt Bank Buildi...

events.title: When Manilatown Swung: The Manila Serenaders
events.description:
Manilatown Heritage FoundationWHEN MANILATOWN SWUNG: THE MANILA SERENADERS
What did Manilatown sound like when Kearny Street was alive with music?
Step into the sounds and stories of historic Manilatown for a special Club Mandalay: Music, Memory & Manilatown gathering featuring live jazz, archival photographs, family memories, and community Talk Story at the International Hotel Manilatown Center.

At the heart of the afternoon is Canuto Salaver, a drummer with the Manila Serenaders whose life was deeply connected to historic Manilatown and the I-Hotel. Members of the Salaver Family join guest interviewer Sabrina Oliveros to share family stories passed down about Canuto-his life around Kearny Street, his connection to the Bataan Cafe and Poolhall, and his years making music with the Manila Serenaders.
The musical lineage continues with Raymond Bambao, bassist with today’s Manilatown Jazz Ensemble, whose grandfather and grand-uncles also played with the Manila Serenaders.
Throughout the afternoon, the Manilatown Jazz Ensemble brings these histories back into sound with live musical interludes inspired by the era, while photographs and materials from the Manilatown Archives and family collections bring the world of historic Manilatown into view.
Audience members will also be invited into the Talk Story-because the memories carried by our families and communities are part of how history lives.
And because history can be fun: Feeling festive? Come dressed in your 1930s-40s finest!...

Adults 21+, $40, Members receive $15 off
Immersive Trek

As the sun dips below the horizon and shadows stretch through the forest, the Halloween Hike begins! Join us for a moderate, 75–90 minute spine-tingling adventure through the darkened trails of the majestic Oakland Redwood forest, where ghostly tales and eerie surprises await.
Led by our spooky expert guides, this haunted trek combines the thrill of exploration with chilling stories sure to give you goosebumps. Dare to venture into the night and uncover the secrets hidden among the trees. Come in costume to add to the fun—you might even receive an extra treat! Enjoy a beautiful sunset hike:
Immersive Trek: 5 PM, between 2.5-3.5 miles, approximately 120 minutes.

Tickets include two drink tickets (beer, wine, or non-alcoholic beverages) and refreshments. This program is for adults 21+.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.title: One City One Book: Cities as Ancestors (SF Main Library)
events.venue: San Francisco Main Library, Koret Auditorium
events.description:
San Francisco Public LibraryExplore how our relationships with cities, parks and the more-than-human world can shape our future. Inspired by Susanna Kwan’s Awake in the Floating City, the 2026 One City One Book selection, this conversation brings together local community leaders working on place-based environmental justice to consider what it means to be an ancestor and how the places we inhabit become part of our collective legacy.
Drawing on five years of the Parks as Ancestors series, inspired by the book, What Kind of Ancestor Do You Want to Be?, the discussion expands the conversation beyond protected parklands to consider urban spaces as living legacies.
This interactive program invites participants to consider what we inherit from the places and people who came before us-and what we will leave behind for those who come after. Attendees are welcome to bring a photograph or a sentimental object honoring someone they have lost, if they wish to incorporate it into the program.

Presented by San Francisco Public Library
