Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.title: Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
events.description:
Yerba Buena Illuminated: Free 95-Ft Art Projection on Market Street
Yerba Buena Partnership
San Francisco has officially turned a downtown building into a giant art projector.

Yerba Buena Illuminated launched Tuesday, August 25, 2026 projecting giant digital artworks onto the historic Humboldt Bank Building at 785 Market St., at the top of Yerba Buena Lane. The massive projection covers a 95-foot-high by 46-foot-wide section of the building, turning one of Market Street’s historic facades into a giant outdoor art screen.

The free outdoor art show runs nightly from twilight until 10 p.m., with the first artwork on view for about 90 days. The inaugural projection is Jennifer Steinkamp’s It’s a nice day for a white wedding. (2008), from SFMOMA’s collection. Inspired by Billy Idol’s “White Wedding,” the digital artwork covers the Beaux-Arts-style building with a cascade of animated red, white and yellow wedding flowers.

The project is a collaboration between Yerba Buena Partnership, SFMOMA, the Museum of the African Diaspora and Yerba Buena Center for the Arts. And this first installation is just the beginning: MoAD and YBCA will curate future projections in 2027, so the giant building-as-canvas is sticking around.
The projection is designed to serve as a giant welcome sign for the Yerba Buena arts district, home to more than 60 public artworks and some of San Francisco’s biggest cultural institutions. The rotating projections will continue to light up the Humboldt Bank Buildi...

events.title: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong
events.description: Submitted by the Event OrganizerThe UC TheatreFor Pigeons Playing Ping Pong, music is a living flame—one demanding relentless tending, fresh kindling, and the collective breath of community to sustain it. On their eighth studio album, Feed The Fire (No Coincidence Records), the Baltimore quartet—“Scrambled Greg” Ormont [vocals, guitar], Jeremy Schon [guitar, vocals], Ben Carrey [bass, vocals], and Alex “Gator” Petropulos [drums, vocals]—push their psychedelic funk odyssey into its most expansive incarnation yet. Across sixteen years, eight albums, and countless sweat-soaked performances, Pigeons have mastered transformation, deepening their connection with their devoted fanbase and channeling life’s seismic shifts into fuel for their unquenchable fire. “The ‘fire’ represents our passion,” explains Ormont. “Making music feels like something we were born to do… Feed The Fire is the perfect metaphor for our unwavering commitment to keep evolving.” Significant milestones, from headlining major stages to their fan-centric Domefest, underscore their remarkable journey.

events.title: Free Behind-the-Scenes Talk: How SF Neo-Futurists Run 100 Shows a Year (SF Main Library)
events.venue: SFPL Main Library Steve Silver Room (4th Floor)
events.description:
SF Neo-FuturistsLearn what it takes to write, direct and perform 100 SHOWS A YEAR as a small group of artists who also RUN THE BUSINESS together. It’s not a sitcom, it’s The San Francisco Neo-Futurists. They put on the Infinite Wrench, the show the SF Chronicle calls one of “22 San Francisco things everyone must do!”
They’ll pull back the curtain on how they operate as a non-hierarchical consensus-based collective to organize performance space, run committees, budget and raise funds and ultimately put on a show every week. They’ll also cover their process for writing new material for a new cast of performers to put on a different show every Friday and Saturday night.
The SF Neos are a collective of wildly prolific artists dedicated to the perpetual creation of experimental theatre that is immediate, ephemeral, accessible and cheap. They believe the stage is an extension of daily life: they perform as themselves in a non-illusory, interactive style that challenges the audience to create alongside them as active participants with a voice of their own. They respect and uplift each other on and off stage through non-hierarchical accountability, collective decision-making and anti-oppression practice of all kinds.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

San Francisco Zoo & GardensSan Francisco Zoo & Gardens is thrilled to announce its all-new, two-month-long ZooLights evening holiday program that will light up the Zoo in spectacular fashion from November 6 through January 3, 2027. The nighttime event represents the return of ZooLights, which the Zoo last hosted in 2018.

“The Zoo is the perfect venue for a safe, outdoor holiday lights experience,” said Cassandra Costello, CEO and Executive Director. “We have taken this event to the next level, creating 14 dazzling zones, with winter, botanical or animal-themed components. It’s going to be truly breathtaking, and a great experience for the entire family.”

In addition to traditional holiday zones, where guests will walk through awe-inspiring lighted tunnels and stroll among giant candy canes, giant ornaments and gift boxes, there’s an entire frozen zone, with 10-foot-tall icicles, sparkling snowflakes, a frozen forest, a massive ice throne and frozen sleigh for that perfect family photo.

“The effect will be magical,” said Costello. “Overall, ZooLights will have more than one million lights, and the walk-through areas include amazing photo ops, and nods to the City of San Francisco with a Golden Gate Bridge and the iconic cable car.”

Whimsical animal shapes and scenes will dot the landscape, using 2D and 3D illuminations of a rhino and gorilla, even a tree full of ring-tailed lemurs. Vibrantly colored, larger-than-life butterflies are part of an enchanting botanical pathway,...

events.title: San Francisco Bike Party (First Fridays)
events.description:
San Francisco Bike Party (First Fridays)
San Francisco Bike Party
San Francisco Bike Party (not to be confused with Critical Mass) is a monthly celebration of biking for riders of different ages, types, and skill levels to enjoy. Every month is a different theme and you’re encouraged to dress up.
San Francisco Bike Party is held on the first Friday at 8:00 pm every month (meet at 7:30p, roll at 8p). The starting location and route also changes every month. Check SF Bike Party’s Facebook page for updates.
The rides are fun and safe with stops to dance and socialize along the way. You’ll follow planned routes exploring all different parts of the city each month. They encourage people to bring positivity and contribute to good times while being respectful to others.

Who runs it? Created by a co-op, by and for bike enthusiasts, run by volunteers who plan the routes, test ride them, help participants ride in control, avoid traffic disruption, and not get lost. How SFBP rides: – Stay in the right lane – Stop at red lights – Leave no trace – Ride predictably and in control – Roll past conflict – Ride prepared – When in doubt, “bike party!!”
Updated 5/6/22 – Event info last checked via Facebook and Instagram

events.description: Presidio TrustJoin us at the Presidio Tunnel Tops for a family-friendly Día de los Muertos & Diwali event in the park. A free sandwich, salad, or drink and pastry from Another Cafe, ready when the cleanup ends

Everyone is welcome, including first-timers, families, and drop-ins. Check in with a QR code when you arrive. (Comedy tickets are for volunteers 18+.)
Organized by neighborhood volunteers in partnership with Civic Joy Fund and SF Public Works.

events.description:

freeoaklandup
Free Oakland UP, a Social Practice Project by Jocelyn Meggait, is open Fridays through Sundays from 12–4 PM, offering free materials for art, collage, and junk journals such as ephemera, electronics parts, books, and household goods. Outdoor items are entirely free to take (just don’t take their tables, bins or shelves), while indoor visitors can choose one free item per person per day, with additional items available for a monetary donation. Some plants and select treasures are for sale. The shop aims to keep usable items out of the landfill.

events.description:
Film still from "Leap!"

2026 San Francisco Dance Film Festival presents:

Leap!

A runaway hit with families at last year’s festival, Leap! is back by popular demand!

Sunday, November 8 at 1:30PM
Brava Theater
Suggested Donation: $10-15

REGISTER TODAY

Bring the whole family for a free screening of the animated feature film Leap!, a heartwarming adventure about courage, friendship, and following your dreams. Set in 19th-century Paris, the story follows Félicie, a spirited orphan determined to become a ballerina, and her best friend Victor, an aspiring inventor. Together they escape their orphanage and chase their passions in the City of Lights, where Félicie must summon all her determination to pursue the role of a lifetime at the Paris Opera Ballet.
Perfect for aspiring young artists, this event will include an introduction by San Francisco Ballet Principal Dancer Dores André and a short opportunity for participants to dance onstage after the screening.
Admission is free, with a suggested donation of $10/child and $15/adult. Registration is required.

events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerCasa Círculo CulturalRedwood City’s beloved Día de los Muertos celebration returns to downtown on Sunday, November 8, 2026, bringing the community together at Courthouse Square for a vibrant celebration of remembrance, heritage, and culture. Hosted by Casa Círculo Cultural and the San Mateo County History Museum, in collaboration with the Redwood City Parks & Arts Foundation, the annual celebration invites visitors to experience the traditions and evolving cultural expressions of Día de los Muertos in the heart of Redwood City.
This year’s celebration is inspired by Tlaxcala, a region of Mexico rich in Indigenous heritage, history, and vibrant traditions. Each year, Casa Círculo Cultural selects a region or theme of Latin America with a meaningful connection to Día de los Muertos, using its customs, colors, and symbolism to honor those who came before us and explore the enduring connection between past and present.

Taking place at Courthouse Square on Broadway Street between Hamilton Street and Middlefield Road, the celebration will offer a colorful and immersive experience centered on remembrance and community. Visitors will discover vibrant sugar skulls, marigolds, and dozens of family altars, each offering a personal tribute and telling the stories of loved ones who have passed. events.address: 75 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA
events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

events.description:
$5 Off Tix: San Francisco Playhouse’s “Peter Pan Goes Wrong” (Sept. 26-Nov. 28)
San Francisco Playhouse
By Henry Lewis, Henry Shields & Jonathan Sayer The Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society is back, and this time they’re taking on Peter Pan. Save $5 off tickets with code FUNCHEAP.
It’s their most ambitious production yet, complete with flying rigs, sword fights, and a very real crocodile problem. What could possibly go wrong? events.title: Echoes of the Seasons: A Piano Dialogue Between East and West
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSFPLExplore how Eastern and Western composers interpret the seasons across different musical traditions. Western selections express vivid natural imagery, from Vivaldi’s dynamic storms to Tchaikovsky’s romantic winter scenes and the reflective mood of Autumn Leaves. These works translate the physical world into sound through color, emotion and narrative.
Eastern musical philosophy centers Yijing (意境), an aesthetic that blends atmosphere, poetry and spiritual resonance. Rooted in the Chinese pentatonic scale, this approach moves beyond direct depiction, inviting listeners to experience nature as a contemplative reflection of the self.

Through classical masterworks, jazz and traditional Chinese repertoire, this lecture‑recital highlights how artistic languages encounter one another across cultures. The program invites audiences to hear how different musical philosophies interpret the seasons and how these perspectives generate deeper understanding of memory, place and expression.

events.description:

freeoaklandup
Free Oakland UP, a Social Practice Project by Jocelyn Meggait, is open Fridays through Sundays from 12–4 PM, offering free materials for art, collage, and junk journals such as ephemera, electronics parts, books, and household goods. Outdoor items are entirely free to take (just don’t take their tables, bins or shelves), while indoor visitors can choose one free item per person per day, with additional items available for a monetary donation. Some plants and select treasures are for sale. The shop aims to keep usable items out of the landfill.

Plants and select treasures are for sale to help pay for rent and expenses. Thank you for keeping treasures out of the landfill._

events.description:
Japanese Tea Garden’s Free Admission Hour (Golden Gate Park)
Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

Please note that hours and costs change frequently.

Japanese Tea Garden
The Japanese Tea Garden provides visitors from around the world with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty, tranquility, and harmony of a Japanese-style garden in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park.
Originally created as a “Japanese Village” exhibit for the 1894 California Midwinter International Exposition, the Japanese Tea Garden endures as one of the most popular attractions in San Francisco, featuring classic elements such as an arched drum bridge, pagodas, stone lanterns, stepping stone paths, native Japanese plants, serene koi ponds, and a zen garden. Cherry blossom trees bloom throughout the garden in March and April.
Admission to the Japanese Tea Garden is free for San Francisco residents with valid ID. Free hours for everyone (even non-residents) are 9-10 am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

The Downtown PresidiGo does not operate on federal holidays.

Midnight Mystery Ride
Every third Saturday, you are invited to bicycle with the San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride as they set out to a new mystery location in SF.
Where to meet? They’ll post ride start locations on their website and Facebook page, the day of the ride only; there’s no advance warning. The ride happens every third Saturday.
Participants are expected to:

Meet at a local bar before midnight on Saturday
Depart for a ride at midnight
Bring provisions for sharing at ride destination
Be awesome.

Ride start locations will be posted to their website the day of the ride. Only the ride leader knows where they’re going, so bring your sense of adventure. Rides are strictly NRLB (No Rider Left Behind) and generally around 5 miles – all levels of cyclist are welcome. They ride rain or shine.

Located in beautiful Golden Gate Park, the de Young Museum is a landmark art museum founded in 1895. Also, stroll through the whimsical Barbro Osher Sculpture Garden to see modern works and James Turrel’s site-specific sculpture Skyspace.
Access to both the Observation Tower and the Sculpture Garden are free to the public. Please note, the Tower Observation Level closes one hour before the museum closes.

events.title: San Francisco Bike Party (First Fridays)
events.description:
San Francisco Bike Party (First Fridays)
San Francisco Bike Party
San Francisco Bike Party (not to be confused with Critical Mass) is a monthly celebration of biking for riders of different ages, types, and skill levels to enjoy. Every month is a different theme and you’re encouraged to dress up.
San Francisco Bike Party is held on the first Friday at 8:00 pm every month (meet at 7:30p, roll at 8p). The starting location and route also changes every month. Check SF Bike Party’s Facebook page for updates.
The rides are fun and safe with stops to dance and socialize along the way. You’ll follow planned routes exploring all different parts of the city each month. They encourage people to bring positivity and contribute to good times while being respectful to others.

Who runs it? Created by a co-op, by and for bike enthusiasts, run by volunteers who plan the routes, test ride them, help participants ride in control, avoid traffic disruption, and not get lost. How SFBP rides: – Stay in the right lane – Stop at red lights – Leave no trace – Ride predictably and in control – Roll past conflict – Ride prepared – When in doubt, “bike party!!”
Updated 5/6/22 – Event info last checked via Facebook and Instagram

events.title: Drawing From Film—Night of the Hunter
events.description:
Submitted by the Event OrganizerSFPLWe’ll be pausing Laughton’s Southern Gothic thriller, Night of the Hunter, to draw striking frames. We’ll be focusing on the art deco design, dramatic shadows and poses in the film.
Basic materials (pencils, paper, erasers) will be provided. You may bring your own materials, but please no fume-creating paint or paint pens. Watercolor, ink and gouache are fine.

This is a self-led event; there will be no instruction or feedback. However, there will be an opportunity at the end of the session to look at others’ drawings and show your own.
PG, 92 mins., 1955. Closed captions (CC) in English. Due to pauses for drawing, the full film will not be shown.
The event takes places in the Main Library at 100 Larkin Street, in the Latino/Hispanic Meeting Room.

events.title: Performance: Kim Shuck’s Poem Celebrates November Dance Shirt
events.venue: San Francisco Public Library, Main Library, Latino Room (lower level)
events.description:
K. ShuckSan Francisco Poet Laureate emerita Kim Shuck, poet Lauren Ito and special guests celebrate Shuck’s new collection November Dance Shirt at SFPL’s Monthly poetry reading.
Kim Shuck was San Francisco’s seventh Poet Laureate. Her poetry draws on her multiethnic background which includes Polish and Cherokee heritage, and her experiences as a lifelong resident of San Francisco. Her most recent book of poetry, November Dance Shirt, was published in 2026, and her book of essays, Noodle, Rant, Tangent, was published in 2022. In her term as Poet Laureate, she hosted scores of free poetry and art workshops for all ages at neighborhood libraries and schools and worked closely with San Francisco Public Library and the San Francisco Arts Commission to launch major citywide initiatives to honor Native American Indigenous Peoples’ heritage.

events.description:
San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride (Every Third Saturday)
Midnight Mystery Ride
Every third Saturday, you are invited to bicycle with the San Francisco Midnight Mystery Ride as they set out to a new mystery location in SF.
Where to meet? They’ll post ride start locations on their website and Facebook page, the day of the ride only; there’s no advance warning. The ride happens every third Saturday.
Participants are expected to:

Meet at a local bar before midnight on Saturday
Depart for a ride at midnight
Bring provisions for sharing at ride destination
Be awesome.

Ride start locations will be posted to their website the day of the ride. Only the ride leader knows where they’re going, so bring your sense of adventure. Rides are strictly NRLB (No Rider Left Behind) and generally around 5 miles – all levels of cyclist are welcome. They ride rain or shine.

Spend the evening exploring more than 100 whiskies from around the world while enjoying the outdoor setting of History Park, live music, food, and whiskey education.
Guests can meet distillers, discover the stories behind different whiskies, compare flavors, and enjoy pours representing regions including Scotland, Ireland, Japan, Texas, and beyond.

Whether you’re a longtime whiskey enthusiast or simply curious to learn more, Whiskey in the Park brings together whiskey, food, music, education, and community for an evening in San Jose.

Time: 5:00 PM–10:00 PM

events.title: Fall Family Festival
events.description:
Taking place under the twinkling Spectra lights, the Fall Family Festival on October 17th, from 4 to 7pm; features fun carnival games, free pumpkin decorating, face painting, the San Francisco Public Library Bookmobile, and entertainment such as stilt walkers and bubble magic with Sterling Bubbles.
The selfie station with the autumn-themed Petalz Flower Truck is a must stop photo op with City Hall as the backdrop, as are the carnival treats: cotton candy, candy apples and local food trucks featuring fall fair favorites.
Sign up on Eventbrite for an event day reminder, but no ticket needed to attend this free event.
This event is sponsored by: Avenue Greenlight, an investment engine for San Francisco’s community projects, providing high-impact grants with tangible results; along with Civic Center Community Benefit District, Illuminate, the San Francisco Public Library and San Francisco Recreation & Parks Department.

Also be sure to check out adjacent kid & family events, San Francisco District Attorney’s Office‘s Keepin’ It Safe in the City (Civic Center Plaza, 10am-2pm) and Market Street Arts‘ Market Street Arts & Theater Festival (many locations, including UN Plaza, with circus and aerial performances in the evening, event runs 4-10pm).

events.description: Visit the pop up pumpkin patch sprouting in Civic Center Plaza on Wednesday, October 28, 9am-4pm. From Compass Family Services, all area neighborhood kids are welcome; expect activities, treats, entertainment and, of course, pumpkins!

events.title: Performing Arts Showcase
events.description:
On Friday, November 13, from 5–8 pm, Fulton Plaza will come alive beneath the dazzling SPECTRA lights for the holiday season’s Performing Arts Showcase, a celebration bringing together some of downtown’s most exciting performing arts organizations for one unforgettable evening.
Guests will be treated to a dynamic lineup of live performances of what’s on stage Fall 2026-Winter 2027. Expect short works from the San Francisco Opera, San Francisco Ballet, San Francisco Conservatory of Music, the African American Shakespeare Company, RAW Dance, and more. From powerful voices and sweeping orchestral music to captivating movement and theatrical performances, the showcase offers a little bit of everything — and is a memorable way to launch the holiday season.
This event is free, RSVP here.
The event also includes an opportunity to mingle with performers and representatives from performing arts organizations, ticket sales, ticket giveaways from the SF Symphony and Orpheum Theatre, and delicious bites and drinks for purchase.
Thank you to event sponsors: Avenue Greenlight, Civic Center Community Benefit District, Illuminate, and the San Francisco Public Library

More information to come.

events.title: Richard Howell’s John Coltrane Tribute
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description: The 100th anniversary of John Coltrane’s birthday has inspired dozens of performances across the Bay Area this year, but no artist is better equipped to evoke the legacy of the saxophone titan and spiritual seeker than Richard Howell. An acclaimed musician, composer and educator, he defines his performances as “Bridge Music,” a jazz pathway that creates sonic connection across obstacles and differences. It’s music that celebrates diversity as it bridges, unites and merges the experience of all listeners, an approach rooted in the spirit of John Coltrane’s “A Love Supreme.” Howell, who spent years on the road with Etta James, also embraces the contradiction of James Brown’s simple yet intricate African-inspired rhythmic concepts and the deep soulfulness of the Isley Brothers. As a saxophonist and vocalist, he has a gift for connecting to multi-generational audiences with an abiding spirituality that invites all listeners to partake. He’s particularly eager to present an afternoon honoring the spirit and music of John Coltrane, he explains. “I’ve had the blessing of a close relationship with his son, Ravi Coltrane, as my son Elé has been part of Ravi’s rhythm section as a drummer for the past seven years. What I’m envisioning is an acoustic jazz quartet – tenor saxophone, acoustic piano, bass and drums – rooted in the Coltrane tradition, but also reflecting the living continuum of that music.”

events.title: Joe Bataan
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
Free RSVP
Opening Set from MeloDious

Festival favorite Joe Bataan, a Latin music legend since the mid-1960s, returns to the Gardens for his third performance in the past four years. He made an indelible mark as one of the early stars of Fania Records with a seductive combination of doo-wop vocals and boogaloo, one of the era’s defining sounds. Born Bataan Nitollano to a Filipino father and African-American mother and raised in Spanish Harlem, he is the father of the Latin soul sound, crooning hits like “Gypsy Woman” and “Ordinary Guy.” But Bataan never stayed in one groove for long. He went on to expand his sound in the ’70s with his Ghetto Records releases, co-coining the apt moniker “salsoul,” though he adapted to changing currents at the end of the decade with forays into disco and hip-hop (scoring the early rap hit “Rap-O Clap-O” in 1979). Stepping back from performing in the early ‘80s, he largely disappeared from the scene while working as a youth counselor in detention facilities. It’s a dramatic story that he recounts with humor and searing detail in his 2024 memoir Streetology: The Legacy of the Afro-Filipino, King of Latin Soul. Since returning to music in 2005, he’s reclaimed his crown and is still going strong in his 80s, a fact made evident by his triumphant YBG Festival performances.

The last time MeloDious appeared at the Gardens the group was serving as house band for Cava Menzies’ glorious CO-LLAB choir in 2024. This year the rapidly ascending Oakland trio...

events.title: Afro-Filipino Jazz Project
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
Free RSVP
Few artists have appeared at the Festival more frequently than flutist, percussionist and arranger John Calloway. Whether he’s leading his own band, performing in the sextet of longtime creative partner John Santos, or directing the Latin Jazz Youth Ensemble of San Francisco, Calloway is a Bay Area icon who’s been at the center of the San Francisco Latin jazz scene for some five decades. But his latest and most personal project yet, the Afro-Filipino Jazz Project, takes his music in a new direction. Founded in 2022 as a creative, interactive space, the Project is intended to bring together Afro Filipinx, African American and Filipino American musicians to explore a broad range of musical styles, with a particular emphasis on jazz idioms, African American roots and traditional and folkloric Filipino music. It’s one component of the larger Afro-Filipino Project, a platform dedicated to highlighting and celebrating, individually and collectively, the art practices and artists of the African American and Filipino American communities whose contributions have profoundly shaped our nation’s artistic narrative. For this performance the AFJP features bass star Marcus Shelby, inveterately grooving drummer Deszon Claiborne, Latin jazz piano specialist Murray Low, saxophonist TJ Milan, Conrad Benedicto on kulintang, vocalist and dancer Ting Alvarez and guest vocalist Anna Maria Flechero.

events.title: Bhangra & Beats Night Market
events.address: Yerba Buena Gardens, Mission St. between 3rd & 4th Sts., San Francisco, CA, 94103, United States
events.description:
San Francisco’s biggest South Asian celebration is back, and for the first time ever, it lands at Yerba Buena Gardens, one of downtown’s most iconic arts and cultural destinations.
On July 24 and November 13, Yerba Buena Gardens, Jessie Square, and Yerba Buena Lane will transform into a vibrant, open-air celebration of music, dance, food, and culture—bringing together community, creativity, and connection in the heart of downtown.
As the only outdoor celebration of its size and scale in the Bay Area dedicated to South Asian culture, Bhangra & Beats continues to create a space that is both rooted in tradition and alive with the energy of the Bay.
At the heart of it all is the vibrant Bhangra & Beats atmosphere, a family-friendly celebration where traditional Punjabi rhythms meet Bay Area energy. Non Stop Bhangra collective will once again lead the experience with its signature mix of interactive dance lessons, beautiful performances, live dhol drumming, DJs, and an open dance floor, all flowing into a lively marketplace with food vendors, local makers, community activations, restaurant and bar specials, and family-friendly activities.
Come for the music, stay for the energy. Whether you’re dancing, eating, shopping, or just taking it all in, there’s something here for everyone.
Free RSVP coming soon.
